title: 267: Wales: The Roar of the Red Dragon

sentences.en: Hello, welcome to The Restless History on the day that England are playing Wales, and I think it's time for a sing-song.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎收听《余下的历史》（The Restless History）。今天英格兰队要对阵威尔士队，我想是时候来上一曲了。

sentences.en: That was the opening verse of Amma Ahid by Daphid Ifan.
sentences.zh: 刚才那是达菲德·伊凡（Daphid Ifan）演唱的《我们依然在此》（Amma Ahid）的开篇歌词。

sentences.en: It's become very much the kind of the great theme for Welsh football.
sentences.zh: 这首歌已经成为了威尔士足球的一首伟大主题曲。

sentences.zh: 我相信今天下午看台上一定会响起这首歌。

sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我得把这首歌送给你，因为我猜你对威尔士语的造诣还没到能听懂歌词的程度，不过也许我错了。

sentences.zh: 我错了吗？

sentences.zh: 听众们都知道，汤姆，我是个语言大师。

sentences.en: The master of tongues.
sentences.zh: 语言大师。

sentences.en: Well, for those whose Welsh may not enable them to translate it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，对于那些威尔士语水平不足以翻译这段歌词的人来说。

sentences.en: Let me just quickly distance myself from your Welsh pronunciation, just for the...
sentences.zh: 我得赶紧声明一下，我可不认同你的威尔士语发音，只是为了……

sentences.en: Yeah, I just want to put that absolutely on the record.
sentences.zh: 没错，我就是想把这一点明确记录在案。

sentences.en: That's fine.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: Please continue.
sentences.zh: 请继续。

sentences.zh: 你是什罗普郡人。

sentences.en: You are entitled to say that.
sentences.zh: 你有权那么说。

sentences.en: So the meaning of the words, you don't remember Maxson, nobody knows him.
sentences.zh: 至于歌词的意思，你不记得马克森（Maxson）了，没人认识他。

sentences.en: 1,600 years, a time too long to remember when Magnus Maximus left Wales in the year 383, leaving us a whole nation, and today, look at us.
sentences.zh: 一千六百年了，时间太久，久到人们已经忘记了马格努斯·马克西姆斯（Magnus Maximus）在公元383年离开威尔士时，给我们留下了一个完整的国家，看看今天的我们。

sentences.en: So I think that is a magnificent sentiment.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是一个宏伟的情怀。

sentences.en: Firstly, because as far as I know, it's the only football anthem that mentions the Roman Emperor.
sentences.zh: 首先，据我所知，这是唯一一首提到罗马皇帝的足球赞歌。

sentences.en: Magnus Maximus, yeah.
sentences.zh: 马格努斯·马克西姆斯，没错。

sentences.en: But secondly, Dominic, when he says that nobody knows him, that's not true, because regular listeners to the rest of his history will remember Magnus Maximus,
sentences.zh: 但其次，多米尼克，当他说没人认识他时，那是不对的，因为《余下的历史》的忠实听众会记得马格努斯·马克西姆斯，

sentences.en: because we did an episode on the ghostly afterlife of the Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 因为我们做过一期关于罗马帝国幽灵般来世的节目。

sentences.en: We did, yes.
sentences.zh: 我们确实做过。

sentences.en: And we talked about how the Welsh princes over the early Middle Ages and into the final extinction of Welsh independence under Edward I,
sentences.zh: 我们谈到了威尔士王公们在中世纪早期，一直到爱德华一世统治下威尔士独立最终灭亡之前，

sentences.en: that they preserved this memory that they were kind of descended from...
sentences.zh: 他们是如何保留了这种记忆，即他们某种程度上是……的后裔。

sentences.en: They had this Roman lineage, that they were princes by virtue of having been appointed to their rank by Magnus Maximus,
sentences.zh: 他们拥有这种罗马血统，他们之所以成为王公，是因为被马格努斯·马克西姆斯任命，

sentences.en: who is this Roman general who stripped the island of its legions and went to Gaul and perished.
sentences.zh: 也就是那位抽调了岛上军团、前往高卢并最终战死的罗马将军。

sentences.en: And so that sense of the Welsh as a Roman people in opposition to the English who were barbarians was very strong.
sentences.zh: 因此，威尔士人作为罗马民族，与作为野蛮人的英格兰人相对立的意识非常强烈。

sentences.en: You made an incredible claim at the end of that episode, didn't you, that the last Roman Emperor was Prince Charles, as it was.
sentences.zh: 你在那期节目的最后提出了一个惊人的观点，不是吗？你说最后一位罗马皇帝其实是查尔斯王子。

sentences.en: Because the argument was that Edward I, when he appoints his son, the future Edward II, as Prince of Wales, is kind of appropriating that tradition.
sentences.zh: 因为论点是，爱德华一世在任命他的儿子、未来的爱德华二世为威尔士亲王时，某种程度上是在挪用这一传统。

sentences.en: And it's been handed down through the heirs of the British monarch right the way to the present day.
sentences.zh: 这一传统一直传到了今天英国君主的继承人手中。

sentences.en: And, of course, there is a slight tension in the role played by the current Prince of Wales, who is Prince William, who's always been very,
sentences.zh: 当然，现任威尔士亲王威廉王子的角色存在一点点张力，他一直非常……

sentences.en: very out and proud as an England football fan.
sentences.zh: 非常公开且自豪地支持英格兰足球队。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's been lots of controversy about this in recent days, Tom, because quite a few Welsh fans, the actor Michael Sheen, prominent among them,
sentences.zh: 是的，汤姆，最近几天关于这件事有很多争议，因为相当多的威尔士球迷，其中以演员迈克尔·辛（Michael Sheen）为首，

sentences.en: have been lambasting him and saying, how can you be Prince of Wales and be supporting England?
sentences.zh: 一直在抨击他，说你怎么能既是威尔士亲王又支持英格兰队呢？

sentences.en: And his sort of, you know, classic House of Windsor fudge is to say, I'm supporting both.
sentences.zh: 而他那种温莎王朝式的经典和稀泥做法就是说，我两边都支持。

sentences.en: I hope they both make it to the final and then I'll decide.
sentences.zh: 我希望他们都能打进决赛，到时候我再决定。

sentences.en: And I hope they both win.
sentences.zh: 我希望他们都能赢。

sentences.en: But, Tom, we have managed to do our classic thing, haven't we, of talking for almost five minutes without even mentioning the guest who's been sitting waiting.
sentences.zh: 但是，汤姆，我们又成功地做到了我们那套经典操作，不是吗？聊了快五分钟，却连那位一直在等候的嘉宾都没提。

sentences.en: We have a brilliant gueSt.
sentences.zh: 我们有一位出色的嘉宾。

sentences.en: Very, very patiently.
sentences.zh: 非常有耐心。

sentences.en: So we do have a brilliant gueSt.
sentences.zh: 我们确实有一位出色的嘉宾。

sentences.en: The subject today, as you've explained, is Wales.
sentences.zh: 正如你所解释的，今天的主题是威尔士。

sentences.en: What is Wales?
sentences.zh: 什么是威尔士？

sentences.en: What is Welshness?
sentences.zh: 什么是威尔士性？

sentences.en: And how does it define itself against England?
sentences.zh: 它又是如何通过与英格兰的对比来定义自己的？

sentences.en: The perfect subject for today's match.
sentences.zh: 这是今天这场比赛的完美主题。

sentences.en: And we have the perfect gueSt.
sentences.zh: 我们也有完美的嘉宾。

sentences.en: He is Martin Jones, professor of history at the University of Swansea and the author of the book, Wales, England's Colony.
sentences.zh: 他是马丁·琼斯（Martin Jones），斯旺西大学历史学教授，也是《威尔士，英格兰的殖民地？》（Wales, England's Colony）一书的作者。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the question mark is very important.
sentences.zh: 那个问号非常重要。

sentences.en: The question mark is very important.
sentences.zh: 那个问号非常重要。

sentences.en: So, Martin, welcome to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 那么，马丁，欢迎来到《余下的历史》。

sentences.en: Wales, England's colony or not?
sentences.zh: 威尔士，是英格兰的殖民地吗？

sentences.en: It depends when we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 这取决于我们谈论的是哪个时期。

sentences.en: I wouldn't use the term to describe Wales today as a colony.
sentences.zh: 我不会用“殖民地”这个词来形容今天的威尔士。

sentences.en: But certainly, if you go back to the medieval period, I don't think we can deny that Wales was militarily conquered and subject to colonial laws that put the Welsh in their place.
sentences.zh: 但可以肯定的是，如果你回到中世纪，我认为无法否认威尔士曾被军事征服，并受到殖民法律的束缚，这些法律让威尔士人处于从属地位。

sentences.en: You know, they were second class citizens in their own nation.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们在自己的国家里是二等公民。

sentences.en: So I think, you know, if you want to go that far back, I think it's fine to call Wales maybe England's first colony.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，如果你想追溯到那么久远，我觉得把威尔士称为英格兰的第一个殖民地是可以的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so when we look at the relationship between England and Wales, one of the themes that runs throughout your book is that for most of the history of that relationship,
sentences.zh: 当我们审视英格兰和威尔士之间的关系时，贯穿你书中的一个主题是，在这一关系的大部分历史中，

sentences.en: Wales has defined itself against England, whereas England has not defined itself against Wales.
sentences.zh: 威尔士是通过与英格兰的对比来定义自己的，而英格兰并没有通过与威尔士的对比来定义自己。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: I mean, Wales is a very small nation.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，威尔士是一个非常小的国家。

sentences.en: You know, today it's 3.1 million people.
sentences.zh: 你知道，今天它有310万人口。

sentences.en: And throughout its history, its politics, its culture, its economy has existed in the shadow of England.
sentences.zh: 纵观其历史，它的政治、文化、经济一直存在于英格兰的阴影之下。

sentences.en: And, you know, you could argue that one of the things that brought the different peoples of Wales together, the different medieval kingdoms, was a sense of difference to England.
sentences.zh: 而且，你可以说，将威尔士不同民族、不同中世纪王国团结在一起的因素之一，就是对英格兰的差异感。

sentences.en: You could argue that it was only once those laws that were passed that denied the Welsh civil rights in their own country that they began to feel something in common with each other.
sentences.zh: 你可以说，正是因为那些剥夺了威尔士人在自己国家内公民权利的法律通过后，他们才开始感受到彼此之间的共同点。

sentences.en: The people of Pauys and Gwyneve sort of developed a common identity.
sentences.zh: 波伊斯（Powys）和圭内斯（Gwynedd）的人民发展出了一种共同的身份认同。

sentences.en: You know, this isn't unusual.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这并不罕见。

sentences.en: You know, this happens across history.
sentences.zh: 这在历史上经常发生。

sentences.en: People define themselves against a large neighbour.
sentences.zh: 人们通过与一个强大的邻国对比来定义自己。

sentences.en: The unfortunate thing is that sometimes that can lead to us having a slight chip on our shoulder, maybe not being as confident as we should be as a nation.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，有时这会导致我们产生一点自卑感，也许作为一个国家，我们没有应有的自信。

sentences.en: And, you know, today in Welsh politics, a lot of the argument is about moving beyond that and kind of enjoying Welshness for its own sake,
sentences.zh: 而且，在今天的威尔士政治中，很多争论都是关于超越这一点，享受威尔士性本身，

sentences.en: rather than just because it's different to England.
sentences.zh: 而不是仅仅因为它与英格兰不同。

sentences.en: So the very name Wales, that's a name imposed on Wales from outside, right?
sentences.zh: 那么“威尔士”（Wales）这个名字，是从外部强加给威尔士的，对吧？

sentences.en: It means the strangers or the others or the foreigners.
sentences.zh: 它的意思是“陌生人”、“其他人”或“外国人”。

sentences.en: And that's a name imposed by the English.
sentences.zh: 那是英格兰人强加的名字。

sentences.en: Am I right?
sentences.zh: 我说的对吗？

sentences.en: I mean, imposed suggests that, you know, somebody is coming along and saying, you must take this name.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，“强加”暗示着有人走过来对你说，你必须接受这个名字。

sentences.en: And that isn't happening.
sentences.zh: 事实并非如此。

sentences.en: The origins of the name, you know, are very difficult.
sentences.zh: 这个名字的起源非常复杂。

sentences.en: I mean, when we're going that far back, it's difficult to know exactly what words meant.
sentences.zh: 当我们追溯到那么久远的时候，很难确切知道词语的含义。

sentences.en: And it seems to have different meanings in different contexts.
sentences.zh: 它似乎在不同的语境下有不同的含义。

sentences.en: But at its heart is a sense of difference, of otherness.
sentences.zh: 但其核心是一种差异感，一种他者感。

sentences.en: And that name is given to the people of what we now call Wales by the Anglo-Saxons, although I suppose that's a controversial term in various ways.
sentences.zh: 这个名字是由盎格鲁-撒克逊人赋予我们现在所称的威尔士地区的人民的，尽管我想这个词在各方面都有争议。

sentences.en: Not here.
sentences.zh: 这里没有。

sentences.en: Not on this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 在这个播客里没有。

sentences.en: Not on this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 在这个播客里没有。

sentences.en: So it does take us back to the beginnings of England, the idea of the English.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实把我们带回了英格兰的起源，即“英格兰人”的概念。

sentences.en: And the traditional story is that the Welsh initially define themselves as Britons.
sentences.zh: 传统的故事是，威尔士人最初将自己定义为“布立吞人”（Britons）。

sentences.en: They are the indigenous inhabitants of Britain.
sentences.zh: 他们是不列颠群岛的原住民。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And that sense of the Welsh or British is really important in early Welsh history.
sentences.zh: 那种“威尔士人”或“不列颠人”的意识在早期威尔士历史上非常重要。

sentences.en: There is a strong sense of loss in Welsh history that once they were the owners of this island and then these Germanic peoples came and took it from them.
sentences.zh: 威尔士历史中有一种强烈的失落感，即他们曾经是这座岛屿的主人，然后这些日耳曼民族来了，从他们手中夺走了它。

sentences.en: And within Welsh history, within Welsh legends, there is a very strong idea that one day someone will come back and liberate us from English rule and give us back the island.
sentences.zh: 在威尔士历史和传说中，有一个非常强烈的观念，即总有一天会有人回来，将我们从英格兰的统治下解放出来，把岛屿还给我们。

sentences.en: That idea of sort of the son of prophecy, Amabh de Rogan, is applied to Owen Glyndur in his medieval uprisings against English rule.
sentences.zh: 那种“预言之子”（Amabh de Rogan）的观念被应用到了欧文·格林杜尔（Owen Glyndur）在中世纪反抗英格兰统治的起义中。

sentences.en: But it's also applied to Henry VII, Henry Tudor, who had some Welsh ancestry.
sentences.zh: 但它也适用于亨利七世，亨利·都铎，他有一些威尔士血统。

sentences.en: And when he comes to the English throne, when he takes it after the Battle of Bosworth, there is a sense in Wales that this is Wales now taking back control of their island.
sentences.zh: 当他登上英格兰王位，在博斯沃思战役后夺取政权时，威尔士有一种感觉，即现在是威尔士人夺回他们岛屿控制权的时候了。

sentences.en: And when Henry VII becomes king, he adds to his royal arms the red dragon.
sentences.zh: 当亨利七世成为国王时，他在皇家纹章中加入了红龙。

sentences.en: And that is the kind of the archetype of – if you want to express the story of the conflict between Saxons and Britons, English and Welsh in mythic form,
sentences.zh: 这就是那种原型——如果你想用神话形式表达撒克逊人和布立吞人、英格兰人和威尔士人之间的冲突故事，

sentences.en: the classic account is that Merlin is told of a vision of a red and a white dragon fighting one another.
sentences.zh: 经典的说法是梅林（Merlin）看到了红龙和白龙互相争斗的幻象。

sentences.en: And that in the end, the red dragon chases the white dragon off.
sentences.zh: 最终，红龙把白龙赶走了。

sentences.en: And Merlin says that the red dragon is Wales or the Britons and that the white dragon is the Saxons.
sentences.zh: 梅林说红龙是威尔士人或布立吞人，而白龙是撒克逊人。

sentences.en: And presumably the implication of that in the long run is that the Welsh will get what's now England back.
sentences.zh: 推而广之，其含义大概是威尔士人最终会收复现在的英格兰地区。

sentences.en: Yeah, these stories are really important in Welsh culture right up to the present day in many ways,
sentences.zh: 是的，这些故事在威尔士文化中一直非常重要，直到今天，在许多方面都是如此，

sentences.en: because they tell the Welsh that they're a nation in the face of English conquest, in the face of English oppression, if you want to put it that way.
sentences.zh: 因为它们告诉威尔士人，面对英格兰的征服，面对英格兰的压迫（如果你想这么说的话），他们依然是一个民族。

sentences.en: History gave the Welsh a better story, a story that was confident, a story that was optimistic, a story that made them feel that they were a people.
sentences.zh: 历史给了威尔士人一个更好的故事，一个自信的故事，一个乐观的故事，一个让他们感到自己是一个民族的故事。

sentences.en: So history has been really important in kind of sustaining a sense of Welsh nationhood over the years.
sentences.zh: 所以历史在多年来维持威尔士民族意识方面一直非常重要。

sentences.en: And that idea of perseverance is really important.
sentences.zh: 那种坚韧不拔的精神非常重要。

sentences.en: I mean, the song you mentioned at the beginning of the podcast, Amal Heed, you know, it translates as still here.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你在播客开头提到的那首歌《我们依然在此》，它翻译过来就是“依然在此”。

sentences.en: And the whole message of that song is not really about Maxsen and Roman emperors.
sentences.zh: 那首歌的全部信息其实并不是关于马克森和罗马皇帝。

sentences.en: It's about how Welsh identity has survived through the years.
sentences.zh: 它是关于威尔士身份是如何历经岁月幸存下来的。

sentences.en: As the song says, despite everyone and despite everything, we are still here.
sentences.zh: 正如歌中所唱，尽管有所有人，尽管有所有事，我们依然在此。

sentences.en: And history is so central to Welsh identity.
sentences.zh: 历史在威尔士身份中占据着如此核心的地位。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's really controversial about whether we teach enough of our history in our schools, whether teaching Welsh history is political,
sentences.zh: 而且，关于我们在学校里是否教授了足够的历史，教授威尔士历史是否具有政治性，

sentences.en: whether it's a route to independence.
sentences.zh: 是否是通往独立的一条途径，这些都非常有争议。

sentences.en: But history, you know, history is politicised in Wales and in ways that maybe it's not so much in England.
sentences.zh: 但历史，你知道，历史在威尔士被政治化了，其程度可能在英格兰并不那么明显。

sentences.en: But that identity, that Welsh identity has definitely kind of evolved, hasn't it?
sentences.zh: 但那种身份，那种威尔士身份确实已经演变了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because again, going right back to the beginning, so before the arrival of the Normans, it's the emergence of a unitary kingdom in what becomes England.
sentences.zh: 因为同样地，回到最初，在诺曼人到来之前，在后来成为英格兰的地区出现了一个统一的王国。

sentences.en: That basically pens the Welsh in because the land of England is so much richer than the kind of the more mountainous land of Wales.
sentences.zh: 这基本上把威尔士人困住了，因为英格兰的土地比威尔士多山的土地要富饶得多。

sentences.en: And it means that there's an inevitable discrepancy of power, which presumably has then set the kind of the balance of the relationship for the thousand years that have followed.
sentences.zh: 这意味着存在一种不可避免的权力差异，这大概奠定了随后一千年里这种关系的平衡。

sentences.en: Yeah, geography is really important, I think, to medieval history.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为地理对中世纪历史非常重要。

sentences.en: The mountains are one reason why maybe there wasn't the big push by the Normans into Wales after they take England.
sentences.zh: 山脉是诺曼人征服英格兰后没有大规模推进到威尔士的原因之一。

sentences.en: There are Norman incursions.
sentences.zh: 确实有诺曼人的入侵。

sentences.en: They take low land areas.
sentences.zh: 他们占领了低地地区。

sentences.en: But the mountains were difficult to access.
sentences.zh: 但山脉很难进入。

sentences.en: But also there's less reward for actually taking them.
sentences.zh: 而且实际占领它们的收益也较少。

sentences.en: There's not a lot actually there.
sentences.zh: 那里其实没什么东西。

sentences.en: So the mountains sort of slow the English incursion into Wales.
sentences.zh: 所以山脉减缓了英格兰对威尔士的入侵。

sentences.en: But it also turns Wales into something of a fortress, if you like.
sentences.zh: 但它也把威尔士变成了一座堡垒，如果你愿意这么说的话。

sentences.en: And that helps Welsh identity survive.
sentences.zh: 这有助于威尔士身份的存续。

sentences.en: And that survives down in the subsequent centuries as well, until kind of the romantics of sort of the 18th century start thinking of Wales as a beautiful place.
sentences.zh: 这种存续一直延续到随后的几个世纪，直到18世纪的浪漫主义者开始将威尔士视为一个美丽的地方。

sentences.en: It's a rough, dangerous, rugged place.
sentences.zh: 它是一个粗犷、危险、崎岖的地方。

sentences.en: And there's simply little reason for English visitors to go there.
sentences.zh: 英格兰游客根本没有理由去那里。

sentences.en: And that protects Welsh identity in the Welsh language.
sentences.zh: 这保护了威尔士的身份和威尔士语。

sentences.en: So at this point, we're talking about Welsh identity, the Welsh language, Wales.
sentences.zh: 所以此时，我们正在谈论威尔士身份、威尔士语、威尔士。

sentences.en: How much are those things anachronistic, you know, concepts that we in the 21st century or people in the 20th century were projecting backwards?
sentences.zh: 这些概念在多大程度上是时代错误？你知道，是我们21世纪的人或20世纪的人投射回过去的吗？

sentences.en: So in other words, would people in the 11th century or whatever, or the 12th century, would they have thought of themselves as Welsh, as being one people from north to south,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，11世纪或12世纪的人，他们会认为自己是威尔士人吗？认为自己是从北到南的一个民族，

sentences.en: speaking one language with one culture?
sentences.zh: 说着同一种语言，拥有同一种文化？

sentences.en: I mean, they definitely wouldn't have thought of themselves as Celts, would they?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们肯定不会认为自己是凯尔特人，对吧？

sentences.en: Because that, again, is a more modern invention, I guess.
sentences.zh: 因为那也是一个更现代的发明，我想。

sentences.en: Yeah, Celts, I really don't like the term Celtic, although it's used quite a lot in Wales.
sentences.zh: 是的，凯尔特人，我真的不喜欢“凯尔特”这个词，尽管它在威尔士用得很多。

sentences.en: It's misleading.
sentences.zh: 它具有误导性。

sentences.en: If you go back to the Middle Ages, it's really obviously difficult to know what ordinary people, what peasants thought, because simply nobody asked them and nobody wrote it down.
sentences.zh: 如果你回到中世纪，显然很难知道普通人、农民在想什么，因为根本没人问他们，也没人把它写下来。

sentences.en: But the Lords of Wales do seem to have had a sense of Welshness.
sentences.zh: 但威尔士的领主们似乎确实有一种威尔士意识。

sentences.en: You know, they do talk about Welsh language, about the Welsh culture, the princes of the various kingdoms of Wales talk about Welshness.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们确实谈论威尔士语，谈论威尔士文化，威尔士各个王国的王公们谈论威尔士性。

sentences.en: They make alliances against the English or against the Normans.
sentences.zh: 他们结盟对抗英格兰人或诺曼人。

sentences.en: And it does seem that amongst the ruling class, there is a sense of Welshness.
sentences.zh: 在统治阶级中，似乎确实存在一种威尔士意识。

sentences.en: It coexists alongside a sense of being from Powys or Gwynedd or to Haybarth or any of the other Welsh kingdoMs.
sentences.zh: 它与波伊斯、格温内斯、海巴斯或其他任何威尔士王国的那种归属感并存。

sentences.en: But it does seem to be that a common language and a common law as well do give the Welsh a sense of identity and a sense of difference to the English on the other side of the border.
sentences.zh: 但共同的语言和共同的法律确实赋予了威尔士人一种身份认同感，以及一种与边境另一侧英格兰人截然不同的感觉。

sentences.en: So you, in your wonderful book, Wales, England's Colony,
sentences.zh: 那么，在您那本精彩的著作《威尔士：英格兰的殖民地》中，

sentences.en: you quote the first Norman bishop of St. David's as saying of the Welsh that they are entirely different in nation language, laws and habits, judgments and custoMs.
sentences.zh: 您引用了圣戴维斯第一任诺曼主教的话，他说威尔士人在民族、语言、法律、习惯、审判和习俗方面完全不同。

sentences.en: Presume that is with reference to the English or to the Normans or to the totality of kind of Latin Europe.
sentences.zh: 我想这指的是英格兰人、诺曼人，或者是整个拉丁欧洲。

sentences.en: I mean, who's he comparing them to?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他是在拿谁和他们做比较？

sentences.en: I mean, sort of the English and the Normans get mixed up in this period, don't they?
sentences.zh: 我是说，在这个时期，英格兰人和诺曼人似乎混在一起了，不是吗？

sentences.en: And, you know, it's sometimes hard to distinguish between who's exactly been spoken to about.
sentences.zh: 而且，有时候很难区分到底是在说谁。

sentences.en: But there is that sense of, you know, of a people with habits.
sentences.zh: 但确实存在那种感觉，你知道，一种有着特定习俗的民族的感觉。

sentences.en: And it's important to think that, you know, nationhood in this period isn't just seen as kind of a political unit.
sentences.zh: 而且重要的是要想到，那个时期的民族性不仅仅被视为一种政治单位。

sentences.en: It's about what we today would call race.
sentences.zh: 它关乎我们今天所说的种族。

sentences.en: Because on the topic of political union, really, there's only an eight year period, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 因为谈到政治统一，实际上只有八年的时间，不是吗？

sentences.en: Where there is a kind of Welsh nation rather than a collection of different principalities that are all Welsh.
sentences.zh: 在那期间，存在一种威尔士民族，而不是一系列各自为政的威尔士公国。

sentences.en: Yeah, Wales is divided up into different kingdoMs.
sentences.zh: 是的，威尔士被划分为不同的王国。

sentences.en: You know, they're constantly at war with each other.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们之间不断地发生战争。

sentences.en: They're constantly vying for control.
sentences.zh: 他们不断地争夺控制权。

sentences.en: Which one's most powerful ebbs and flows over the course of the centuries?
sentences.zh: 哪个王国最强大，这在几个世纪里起起伏伏。

sentences.en: But yeah, there is only a kind of an eight year period where you could say all of the kingdoms of Wales are under one ruler.
sentences.zh: 但确实，只有大约八年的时间，你可以说所有的威尔士王国都在同一个统治者之下。

sentences.en: But that doesn't mean that there isn't this sense of the Welsh as a nation, as a people, you know, that there isn't some sense of a common ancestry.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着不存在威尔士作为一个民族、作为一个群体的意识，你知道，不存在某种共同祖先的意识。

sentences.en: And that's where we go back to this idea that once this was our whole island and we are the true Britons and the Anglo-Saxons came and took it from us.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们回到那个想法的地方：曾经整个岛屿都是我们的，我们是真正的布立吞人，而盎格鲁-撒克逊人来了并从我们手中夺走了它。

sentences.en: And now the Normans have come and taken it from us.
sentences.zh: 现在诺曼人又来了，从我们手中夺走了它。

sentences.en: But one day we will return.
sentences.zh: 但总有一天我们会夺回来。

sentences.en: So that king is Grafidap Llewellyn, who is king just before the Norman ConqueSt.
sentences.zh: 那位国王是格鲁菲德·阿普·卢埃林，他在诺曼征服前夕担任国王。

sentences.en: And just as the Norman Conquest is a traumatic experience for the English, so also, of course, is it clearly a very traumatic experience for the Welsh.
sentences.zh: 正如诺曼征服对英格兰人来说是一次痛苦的经历，对威尔士人来说，当然也是一次非常痛苦的经历。

sentences.en: And what is the impact of the coming of the Normans to Britain on the Welsh, on Welsh identity and on the coherence of a kind of political sense of Welshness?
sentences.zh: 诺曼人来到不列颠对威尔士人、威尔士身份以及威尔士政治意识的连贯性产生了什么影响？

sentences.en: Well, the early Norman lords are almost given a free reign in Wales.
sentences.zh: 嗯，早期的诺曼领主在威尔士几乎拥有完全的自由。

sentences.en: You know, there is an opportunity for these barons to kind of set up almost like private enterprises in Wales.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些男爵有机会在威尔士建立几乎类似于私人企业的机构。

sentences.en: You know, the English crown almost says, do what you want over there.
sentences.zh: 你知道，英格兰王室几乎是说，你们在那边想干什么就干什么。

sentences.en: And, you know, gradually individual barons, individual Norman lords take land within Wales.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，逐渐地，个别的男爵、个别的诺曼领主在威尔士境内占领了土地。

sentences.en: So these are the marches.
sentences.zh: 这就是边境地区（Marches）。

sentences.en: They come to be called the marches.
sentences.zh: 它们后来被称为边境地区。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that creates what we call the marches, this kind of border area, which is essentially under Norman rule.
sentences.zh: 这创造了我们所说的边境地区，这种本质上处于诺曼统治下的边界地带。

sentences.en: So the conquest of Wales begins very quickly after the conquest of England.
sentences.zh: 所以对威尔士的征服在征服英格兰后很快就开始了。

sentences.en: And that changes the whole politics of Wales, because suddenly there's this big foe, you know, on your doorstep, which is militarily superior, which has better resources,
sentences.zh: 这改变了整个威尔士的政治，因为突然之间，你的家门口出现了一个强大的敌人，它在军事上更优越，拥有更好的资源，

sentences.en: which is very difficult to beat.
sentences.zh: 而且非常难以击败。

sentences.en: And that creates some sense of unity, I think, between, you know, the existing Welsh kingdoMs.
sentences.zh: 我认为这在现有的威尔士王国之间产生了一种团结感。

sentences.en: But they also become an ally, which the Welsh kingdoms can use in their battles and rivalries between each other.
sentences.zh: 但它们也成为了盟友，威尔士王国可以在彼此的战斗和竞争中使用这种盟友关系。

sentences.en: So the whole politics of not just Wales, but of the whole island is changed by the Norman conqueSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，不仅是威尔士，整个岛屿的政治都被诺曼征服改变了。

sentences.en: I love all this because I'm from the marches, Martin, as a Shropshire boy.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这一切，因为我来自边境地区，马丁，作为一个什罗普郡男孩。

sentences.en: So I grew up in this sort of Wales was just over the horizon, you know, on the other side of the Longmind and the landscape studded with castles.
sentences.zh: 所以我是在这种环境下长大的，威尔士就在地平线那边，你知道，在朗明德山的另一边，风景中点缀着城堡。

sentences.en: And I actually wanted to ask a question about castles,
sentences.zh: 我其实想问一个关于城堡的问题，

sentences.en: because I guess the castles that were built in this period and afterwards are the most celebrated man-made landmarks that stand in Wales.
sentences.zh: 因为我想，在这个时期及以后建造的城堡是威尔士最著名的、矗立在那里的地标性建筑。

sentences.en: But of course, you know, people walk around them today and, you know, people like the Sandbrook family go and buy swords and shields of dragons on and whatnot and really love it.
sentences.zh: 但当然，你知道，人们今天走在它们周围，你知道，像桑德布鲁克一家那样的人会去买剑、盾牌、龙之类的东西，真的很喜欢它。

sentences.en: But they are symbols of, I mean, they really are symbols of oppression, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 但它们是压迫的象征，我的意思是，它们确实是压迫的象征，不是吗？

sentences.en: Of surveillance, of control, of foreign domination.
sentences.zh: 是监视、控制和外国统治的象征。

sentences.en: Or am I being too harsh?
sentences.zh: 还是说我太苛刻了？

sentences.en: That's what they're literally there for.
sentences.zh: 它们存在的目的就是如此。

sentences.en: You know, the very first ones are quite small and they're to kind of implant Norman power over local areas.
sentences.zh: 你知道，最初的那些城堡很小，是为了在当地植入诺曼人的权力。

sentences.en: But the last ones, the ones built by Edward I, you know, they are amongst the grandest medieval structures probably anywhere in the world.
sentences.zh: 但最后建造的那些，由爱德华一世建造的，你知道，它们是世界上最宏伟的中世纪建筑之一。

sentences.en: And I think it's reasonable to say they are far larger than was actually needed from a military point of view.
sentences.zh: 我认为可以合理地说，从军事角度来看，它们远比实际需要的大得多。

sentences.en: So it's very difficult to escape the conclusion that they are symbolic.
sentences.zh: 所以很难逃避这样一个结论：它们具有象征意义。

sentences.en: They are telling the Welsh people, you are a conquered people, but maybe not just telling the Welsh people that, but also maybe reminding other English lords.
sentences.zh: 它们在告诉威尔士人民，你们是被征服的民族，但也许不仅是在告诉威尔士人民，也是在提醒其他英格兰领主。

sentences.en: It's look at the power of the crown, the English crown that we can build these structures.
sentences.zh: 这是在展示王室，英格兰王室的力量，我们可以建造这些建筑。

sentences.en: So the symbolism of them works two ways.
sentences.zh: 所以它们的象征意义是双向的。

sentences.en: And it's left a very complicated relationship with those castles, you know, through the rest of history.
sentences.zh: 这在历史的进程中留下了与这些城堡非常复杂的关系。

sentences.en: Because at one level, they remind the Welsh that there are conquered people, that they remind them of this very difficult history.
sentences.zh: 因为在某种程度上，它们提醒威尔士人他们是被征服的民族，提醒他们这段非常艰难的历史。

sentences.en: But the size of them and the scale of them is also something comforting in some ways, because it's also a reminder we were difficult to beat.
sentences.zh: 但它们的大小和规模在某些方面也令人感到安慰，因为这也提醒人们，我们很难被击败。

sentences.en: And they're also big money spinners, right?
sentences.zh: 而且它们也是巨大的摇钱树，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, they bring in a lot of tourists.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们吸引了很多游客。

sentences.en: Yeah, they're great for our tourism.
sentences.zh: 是的，它们对我们的旅游业很有帮助。

sentences.en: And, you know, but one of the shames is often that actually when you walk around them, you don't really get a sense of the politics behind them.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，但令人遗憾的一点往往是，当你走在它们周围时，你并没有真正感受到它们背后的政治含义。

sentences.en: You know, it's very depoliticised, the narratives.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些叙事被非常彻底地去政治化了。

sentences.en: And of course, the relationship between Wales and England is still happening today.
sentences.zh: 当然，威尔士和英格兰之间的关系至今仍在继续。

sentences.en: And there isn't really any effort made to make that connection with today.
sentences.zh: 而且并没有做出任何努力来建立与当下的联系。

sentences.en: So the most famous castles of all are those that are built by Edward I, who completes the conquest of Wales.
sentences.zh: 所以最著名的城堡是爱德华一世建造的那些，他完成了对威尔士的征服。

sentences.en: And his ring of iron, his ring of iron.
sentences.zh: 还有他的铁环，他的铁环。

sentences.en: Yes, his ring of iron.
sentences.zh: 是的，他的铁环。

sentences.en: And you make the point in the book that one of the things that prompts the conquest of Wales is the fact that the kings of England have lost their lands in Normandy.
sentences.zh: 你在书中指出，促成征服威尔士的原因之一是英格兰国王失去了他们在诺曼底的土地。

sentences.en: And so they now are looking for alternative theatres to kind of throw their weight in.
sentences.zh: 所以他们现在正在寻找其他的舞台来施加他们的影响力。

sentences.en: And so Wales is, you know, he's in the way of the juggernaut.
sentences.zh: 所以威尔士，你知道，它挡在了这个庞然大物的路上。

sentences.en: But you also give the extraordinary statistic that in 1287, under Edward I, a quarter of the entire Welsh male population was serving in Edward's army.
sentences.zh: 但你也给出了一个惊人的统计数据：在1287年，在爱德华一世统治下，整个威尔士男性人口的四分之一在爱德华的军队中服役。

sentences.en: So it's not presumably, it's not just about oppression.
sentences.zh: 所以这大概不仅仅是关于压迫。

sentences.en: It's also about giving the Welsh, or at least elements within Wales, a stake within the new regime.
sentences.zh: 这也是为了给威尔士人，或者至少是威尔士内部的某些阶层，在新政权中提供一份利益。

sentences.en: When any nation, when any place is conquered, there are always local people who work with the political realities that they are faced with.
sentences.zh: 当任何民族、任何地方被征服时，总会有当地人与他们所面临的政治现实合作。

sentences.en: With those probably Welsh peasants serving in the Norman army, did they have any choice about the matter?
sentences.zh: 对于那些在诺曼军队中服役的威尔士农民，他们对此有选择吗？

sentences.en: It's a well-paid job, probably, you know, compared to trying to live off the land.
sentences.zh: 这可能是一份报酬不错的工作，你知道，比起靠土地为生来说。

sentences.en: And if you've suddenly become a conquered people, joining the conqueror is a way of maybe getting some status.
sentences.zh: 如果你突然成为了被征服的民族，加入征服者也许是获得某种地位的一种方式。

sentences.en: It's a way of survival.
sentences.zh: 这是一种生存方式。

sentences.en: And I think there is a danger maybe of us looking back and thinking of these things in black and white.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们回顾过去并以非黑即白的方式思考这些事情可能存在危险。

sentences.en: You know, this is Norman or English versus Welsh.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是诺曼人或英格兰人对抗威尔士人。

sentences.en: Whereas the realities of life for people were quite different.
sentences.zh: 而人们生活的现实却大不相同。

sentences.en: I mean, just survival in the medieval period, you know, against the elements, growing enough food, looking after your family.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，仅仅是在中世纪生存，你知道，对抗自然环境、种植足够的食物、照顾你的家庭。

sentences.en: None of these things were easy.
sentences.zh: 这些事情都不容易。

sentences.en: And just on these people, they spoke Welsh, right?
sentences.zh: 就这些人而言，他们说威尔士语，对吧？

sentences.en: They didn't speak English.
sentences.zh: 他们不说英语。

sentences.en: Are there people speaking English at this point?
sentences.zh: 在这个时候有人说英语吗？

sentences.en: In the early Norman incursions, there are efforts to implant essentially new populations, settler populations.
sentences.zh: 在早期的诺曼入侵中，确实有努力去植入本质上是新的人口，定居者人口。

sentences.en: That happens in Gower near Swansea, and that happens in South Pembrokeshire and in Southwest Wales.
sentences.zh: 这种情况发生在斯旺西附近的高尔，也发生在南彭布罗克郡和西南威尔士。

sentences.en: And those places today are still very Anglicised.
sentences.zh: 而这些地方今天仍然非常英格兰化。

sentences.en: If you look at a map of those areas, the place names are English.
sentences.zh: 如果你看一张这些地区的地图，地名都是英语的。

sentences.en: You know, it's almost like literally the Welsh have been wiped off the map.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这几乎就像威尔士人从地图上被抹去了一样。

sentences.en: Now, what happened to the indigenous population, for want of a better term, is very difficult to know.
sentences.zh: 现在，原住民（如果用一个更好的词的话）发生了什么，很难知道。

sentences.en: Were they forced off their land?
sentences.zh: 他们是被迫离开土地的吗？

sentences.en: Was it relatively empty?
sentences.zh: 当时那里相对空旷吗？

sentences.en: You know, is there some kind of process of maybe even genocide going on?
sentences.zh: 你知道，是否发生了某种类似于种族灭绝的过程？

sentences.en: Well, it's exactly the same questions as haunt the question of what happens in Lowland Britain in the post-Roman period.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这正是困扰后罗马时期低地不列颠所发生之事的同样问题。

sentences.en: I mean, it's really fascinating.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这真的很迷人。

sentences.en: But for Welsh speakers, what are the legal frameworks that are governing them following the completion of the English conquest?
sentences.zh: 但对于威尔士语使用者来说，在英格兰征服完成后，统治他们的法律框架是什么？

sentences.en: It's not about language, first of all.
sentences.zh: 首先，这与语言无关。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, being Welsh is never defined by language.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，身为威尔士人从来不是由语言定义的。

sentences.en: In essence, language was a sign of being Welsh, but it is seen as an ethnic identity.
sentences.zh: 本质上，语言是身为威尔士人的标志，但它被视为一种民族身份。

sentences.en: So it's kind of overtly racial then?
sentences.zh: 所以那是公然的种族主义吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: And, you know, there are attempts by some Welsh people to define themselves as English.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，一些威尔士人试图将自己定义为英格兰人。

sentences.en: You know, they go to local courts and say, oh, no, look at my heritage.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们去当地法院说，哦，不，看看我的血统。

sentences.en: You know, despite my name, I'm actually English.
sentences.zh: 你知道，尽管我的名字是这样，但我实际上是英格兰人。

sentences.en: Because there's something legal restrictions.
sentences.zh: 因为存在一些法律限制。

sentences.en: Because that gave you legal rights.
sentences.zh: 因为这能给你法律权利。

sentences.en: So there are laws passed that denied the Welsh the ability to carry arms, to live in towns, to trade in certain places.
sentences.zh: 所以通过了一些法律，剥夺了威尔士人携带武器、居住在城镇、在某些地方进行贸易的权利。

sentences.en: These aren't always enforced.
sentences.zh: 这些法律并不总是被执行。

sentences.en: You know, in some cases, they're just on the stature book.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在某些情况下，它们只是写在法典上。

sentences.en: And historians have gone through the lists of tenants and people living in Welsh towns and actually shown a fair proportion of them in some places do have Welsh names.
sentences.zh: 历史学家查阅了租户名单和居住在威尔士城镇的人员名单，实际上显示在某些地方，他们中有相当一部分人拥有威尔士名字。

sentences.en: But these laws are there on the books.
sentences.zh: 但这些法律确实存在于法典中。

sentences.en: And that made them people literally second class citizens.
sentences.zh: 这使他们实际上成为了二等公民。

sentences.en: And even if these laws aren't always enforced, they're always there in the background.
sentences.zh: 即使这些法律并不总是被执行，它们也总是存在于背景中。

sentences.en: So if you fall out with your neighbour, you know, and you're making better beer than him, and, you know, your neighbour might say, but hang on, you're Welsh.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你和邻居闹翻了，你知道，你酿的啤酒比他好，而且，你知道，你的邻居可能会说，但等等，你是威尔士人。

sentences.en: You shouldn't even be in this town.
sentences.zh: 你甚至不应该待在这个镇上。

sentences.en: You know, there does seem to be that in the background.
sentences.zh: 你知道，背景中似乎确实存在这种情况。

sentences.en: I don't think it's too far to say that people were literally second class citizens in their own nation.
sentences.zh: 我认为说人们在自己的国家实际上是二等公民并不为过。

sentences.en: And there's no representation in the English Parliament?
sentences.zh: 而且在英格兰议会中没有代表权？

sentences.en: There's no representation in the English Parliament.
sentences.zh: 在英格兰议会中没有代表权。

sentences.en: It can be difficult to work your way up the ladder.
sentences.zh: 想要步步高升可能会很困难。

sentences.en: But, of course, the governance of any nation requires people, officials who speak the local language.
sentences.zh: 但当然，任何国家的治理都需要人，需要说当地语言的官员。

sentences.en: You know, so there are opportunities, career opportunities for ambitious people within the Welsh gentry.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所以对于威尔士绅士阶层中雄心勃勃的人来说，是有机会的，有职业机会的。

sentences.en: And so there's one last kind of great national uprising, which is under Owen Glyndour.
sentences.zh: 所以还有最后一次伟大的民族起义，是在欧文·格林杜尔领导下的。

sentences.en: Glyndour.
sentences.zh: 格林杜尔。

sentences.en: Well, I'm sorry, I'm Henry IV part one-ing because he's a figure in Shakespeare's version of Henry IV's reign.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我很抱歉，我一直在引用《亨利四世》第一部，因为他是莎士比亚版《亨利四世》统治时期的一个人物。

sentences.en: That's a terrible portrait of him, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 那对他来说是一个糟糕的画像，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because he's like a sort of necromancer babbling in Welsh.
sentences.zh: 因为他就像一个用威尔士语胡言乱语的巫师。

sentences.en: He speaks in very florid poetry, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他说话用词非常华丽，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: Harry Hotspur sneers it in.
sentences.zh: 哈里·霍茨珀嘲笑它。

sentences.en: I don't imagine that's a production.
sentences.zh: 我不认为那是一部受欢迎的作品。

sentences.en: That's a Shakespeare production that's welcomed on the streets of Caerphilly or whatever.
sentences.zh: 那是一部在卡菲利或其他地方的街头受欢迎的莎士比亚作品。

sentences.en: Anyway, sorry, go on, Tom.
sentences.zh: 总之，抱歉，继续吧，汤姆。

sentences.en: Ask your question.
sentences.zh: 问你的问题。

sentences.en: But what Shakespeare's treatment also does is offer Prince Hal the future Henry V.
sentences.zh: 但莎士比亚的处理方式也提供了哈尔王子，未来的亨利五世。

sentences.en: He's Henry of Monmouth, and he is cast as someone who can bridge English and Welsh identity.
sentences.zh: 他是蒙茅斯的亨利，他被塑造为一个能够架起英格兰和威尔士身份桥梁的人。

sentences.en: Is that something that is reflective of the Tudor period, by which point we've got a dynasty that claims descent from Wales?
sentences.zh: 这是否反映了都铎王朝时期，那时我们已经有了一个声称来自威尔士的王朝？

sentences.en: Or is that approximating to something that does emerge in the wake of Owen Glyndour's rebellion?
sentences.zh: 还是说这接近于欧文·格林杜尔叛乱后出现的情况？

sentences.en: I mean, there's always the practical politics.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，总有实际的政治考量。

sentences.en: People want to get on in life.
sentences.zh: 人们想要在生活中取得进步。

sentences.en: And Owen Glyndour is a good example of that.
sentences.zh: 欧文·格林杜尔就是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: But, you know, he'd learned, you know, he'd plied his trade in the law in London.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，他学过，你知道，他在伦敦从事法律工作。

sentences.en: He'd served in the English army.
sentences.zh: 他在英格兰军队服役过。

sentences.en: His family, you know, had English connections.
sentences.zh: 他的家族，你知道，有英格兰关系。

sentences.en: Like a lot of the Welsh gentry after conquest, he started to make a career of himself with using the structures of power with England.
sentences.zh: 像征服后许多威尔士绅士一样，他开始利用英格兰的权力结构为自己开创事业。

sentences.en: But something goes wrong.
sentences.zh: 但出了点问题。

sentences.en: He falls out with another landowner.
sentences.zh: 他和另一位地主闹翻了。

sentences.en: And somehow that turns into a national uprising.
sentences.zh: 不知怎么的，这演变成了一场全国性的起义。

sentences.en: There seems to be this undercurrent of resentment about the way Welsh people were treated.
sentences.zh: 威尔士人受到的待遇似乎引发了一种潜在的怨恨情绪。

sentences.en: And Glyndour's rebellion plays upon that, and it draws people out.
sentences.zh: 格林多（Glyndour）的叛乱正是利用了这一点，并吸引了人们参与其中。

sentences.en: And this kind of suppressed sense of anger that people seem to have had about the way Wales was treated bursts into flame.
sentences.zh: 人们对威尔士所受待遇的那种压抑已久的愤怒，瞬间爆发成了熊熊烈火。

sentences.en: And it is an incredibly violent, aggressive uprising.
sentences.zh: 这是一场极其暴力、极具侵略性的起义。

sentences.en: The towns of Wales are burnt because they're symbols of English colonialism, because of these laws about who can live in them.
sentences.zh: 威尔士的城镇被焚毁，因为它们是英国殖民主义的象征，也因为那些关于谁能居住在其中的法律。

sentences.en: It's full-scale kind of civil war in many ways.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，这都是一场全面爆发的内战。

sentences.en: You know, there are open battles as well against the English army.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当时也确实发生了针对英军的公开战役。

sentences.en: This is not a small event.
sentences.zh: 这绝非小事。

sentences.en: And in many ways, it ravages the Welsh economy for the next couple of centuries.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，它在接下来的几个世纪里摧残了威尔士的经济。

sentences.en: And it leaves a degree of bitterness and a degree of anger as well about the way it fizzled out, but also about how ethnic tensions between the Welsh and the English,
sentences.zh: 它留下了一定程度的苦涩和愤怒，不仅是因为起义最终不了了之，也是因为威尔士人和英国人之间的民族紧张关系，

sentences.en: what they can turn into.
sentences.zh: 可能会演变成什么样子。

sentences.en: And I think it does create a sense we can't ever go back to that.
sentences.zh: 我认为这确实让人产生了一种我们再也回不到过去的感觉。

sentences.en: You know, we need to rebuild a future which is cooperation.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们需要重建一个基于合作的未来。

sentences.en: Among the Welsh themselves or with the English crown?
sentences.zh: 是在威尔士人内部，还是与英国王室之间？

sentences.en: Because I'm just asking about Henry V, that, you know, he goes on to win the Battle of Agincourt with the longbow, which is a Welsh weapon.
sentences.zh: 因为我只是想问关于亨利五世的事，你知道，他后来用长弓赢得了阿金库尔战役，那可是威尔士的武器。

sentences.en: And that sense of, is there any sense in the 15th century of English and Welsh identity starting to merge?
sentences.zh: 那么，在15世纪，是否已经有了英国和威尔士身份开始融合的意识？

sentences.en: Or is that just a later back projection that Shakespeare's engaging in?
sentences.zh: 还是说那只是莎士比亚后来的一种投射？

sentences.en: No, there's a degree of reconciliation that, you know, the Welsh gentry are kind of like, we must never go back to this, to what happened in Glyndour's period.
sentences.zh: 不，确实存在一定程度的和解，你知道，威尔士绅士们当时的想法是，我们绝不能重蹈覆辙，不能再发生格林多时期那样的事情。

sentences.en: But the English crown is also, we don't want another uprising.
sentences.zh: 但英国王室也想，我们不希望再发生起义。

sentences.en: And, you know, it doesn't act too harshly after the uprising is crushed.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，起义被镇压后，他们并没有采取过于严厉的手段。

sentences.en: You know, there is some reconciliation.
sentences.zh: 你知道，确实存在一些和解。

sentences.en: There's even some compensation paid to some communities.
sentences.zh: 甚至还向一些社区支付了赔偿金。

sentences.en: But the fact that there are Welsh archers serving in the English army, again, that's part of a much longer history.
sentences.zh: 但威尔士弓箭手在英军中服役这一事实，同样是更长历史的一部分。

sentences.en: And that's much more about individuals wanting to find work in some places.
sentences.zh: 这更多是关于个人在某些地方寻求工作的问题。

sentences.en: You know, so the hiring of foreign mercenaries, the hiring of foreign people by the English army is nothing new.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所以英军雇佣外国雇佣兵、雇佣外国人并不是什么新鲜事。

sentences.en: That didn't need reconciliation between the Welsh and English.
sentences.zh: 那并不需要威尔士和英国之间的和解。

sentences.en: But that is happening slowly.
sentences.zh: 但这确实在缓慢发生。

sentences.en: But when the Tudors come in, you quote a Welsh writer, Owen of Henlis, am I pronouncing that right?
sentences.zh: 但当都铎王朝到来时，你引用了一位威尔士作家，亨利斯的欧文（Owen of Henlis），我发音对吗？

sentences.en: Henlis.
sentences.zh: 亨利斯。

sentences.en: Henlis, who calls Henry the Moses who delivered us from bondage.
sentences.zh: 亨利斯，他称亨利为将我们从奴役中拯救出来的摩西。

sentences.en: And he famously names his son, Arthur, great British hero.
sentences.zh: 他给儿子取名为亚瑟，这可是伟大的不列颠英雄。

sentences.en: And as I mentioned, he adds the red dragon to his coat of arMs.
sentences.zh: 正如我提到的，他在自己的纹章上增加了红龙。

sentences.en: So is there a feeling in Wales that with the Tudors, things genuinely change?
sentences.zh: 那么，威尔士是否有一种感觉，随着都铎王朝的到来，情况真的发生了变化？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Henry Tudor exploits his Welsh ancestry in many ways.
sentences.zh: 亨利·都铎在许多方面利用了他的威尔士血统。

sentences.en: He uses a way of gaining support and manpower within Wales as he's marching towards Bosworth for his battle to seize the English crown.
sentences.zh: 当他向博斯沃思进军以夺取英国王位时，他利用这一点在威尔士获得了支持和人力。

sentences.en: But once he actually has the English crown, he does seem to hold up to some of his promises.
sentences.zh: 但一旦他真正获得了英国王位，他似乎确实兑现了一些承诺。

sentences.en: You know, he brings Welsh people to court.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他把威尔士人带到了宫廷。

sentences.en: He does these symbolic things like, you know, putting the dragon on his heraldry and things like that.
sentences.zh: 他做了一些象征性的事情，比如，你知道，把龙放在他的纹章上之类的。

sentences.en: And there is a sense in Wales, or at least amongst the Welsh people who wrote about these things, the poets and the lords,
sentences.zh: 在威尔士，或者至少在那些书写这些事情的威尔士人——诗人和领主们——心中，确实有一种感觉，

sentences.en: that Wales has retaken its position at the heart of Britain.
sentences.zh: 那就是威尔士已经重新回到了不列颠的核心地位。

sentences.en: That, you know, our previous oppression, our previous shame, our kind of sense of being conquered, that's all in the past now.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们之前的压迫、之前的耻辱、那种被征服的感觉，现在都已成为过去。

sentences.en: Now there is a Welshman on the throne of England and Wales is back in control of this island, just as it should be.
sentences.zh: 现在英格兰王位上坐着一位威尔士人，威尔士重新掌控了这个岛屿，理应如此。

sentences.en: And then there are acts of union just a generation or so later.
sentences.zh: 然后仅仅一代人之后，就出现了《联合法案》。

sentences.en: So under his son, Henry VIII.
sentences.zh: 也就是在他儿子亨利八世统治时期。

sentences.en: So this is driven by Thomas Cromwell, is it?
sentences.zh: 所以这是由托马斯·克伦威尔推动的，是吗？

sentences.en: This is his project of kind of Thomas Cromwell's kind of, Hilary Mantel would call it his kind of social democratic modernization of England and Wales.
sentences.zh: 这是他的计划，希拉里·曼特尔会称之为他那种对英格兰和威尔士的社会民主现代化改造。

sentences.en: So he's trying to smooth out the eccentricities of their relationship to create some new counties, to just get everything in order.
sentences.zh: 所以他试图理顺他们关系中的怪异之处，建立一些新的郡，让一切井然有序。

sentences.en: I mean, is that basically what it's all about?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这基本上就是它的全部意义吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, there's two things driving it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有两件事在驱动它。

sentences.en: There is, I think, a desire for it from some people within Wales.
sentences.zh: 我认为威尔士内部的一些人也有这种愿望。

sentences.en: So even though the Tudors are on the throne now, and even though they're making symbolic gestures towards Wales,
sentences.zh: 所以尽管都铎王朝现在坐在王位上，尽管他们对威尔士做出了一些象征性的姿态，

sentences.en: I think many of the Welsh gentry felt they still weren't fully equal.
sentences.zh: 但我认为许多威尔士绅士觉得他们仍然没有完全平等。

sentences.en: And some of these laws are still there in the background.
sentences.zh: 而且其中一些法律仍然存在于背景中。

sentences.en: So there was a sense that amongst the Welsh gentry that they wanted legal equality with the English.
sentences.zh: 所以威尔士绅士中有一种感觉，他们想要与英国人平等的法律地位。

sentences.en: And the acts of union was a way to achieve that.
sentences.zh: 而《联合法案》就是实现这一目标的一种方式。

sentences.en: But Wales was very complicated administratively.
sentences.zh: 但威尔士在行政上非常复杂。

sentences.en: There were the marchers still, which were under the control of individual English barons.
sentences.zh: 仍然有受个别英国男爵控制的边境地区（Marchers）。

sentences.en: And then there is what was called the Principality of Wales, which was essentially the bit that used to be independent and then got taken by the English crown by Edward I.
sentences.zh: 然后有所谓的威尔士公国，本质上就是曾经独立，后来被爱德华一世夺取的那些部分。

sentences.en: So there's almost like two Walesers.
sentences.zh: 所以几乎有两个威尔士。

sentences.en: And in the Principality, Welsh law is still used.
sentences.zh: 在公国，仍然使用威尔士法律。

sentences.en: In the marches, it's a bit of English law and a bit of Welsh law, really, often according to what would suit the local baron.
sentences.zh: 在边境地区，通常是英国法律和威尔士法律的混合，往往取决于当地男爵的喜好。

sentences.en: And it was administratively complicated.
sentences.zh: 而且在行政上很复杂。

sentences.en: And there was a sense of danger there as well, that, you know, it was a place of crime.
sentences.zh: 那里也有一种危险感，你知道，那是一个犯罪之地。

sentences.en: But of course, also, you know, by this period, the whole question of religion is starting to become important.
sentences.zh: 但当然，你知道，到了这个时期，整个宗教问题也开始变得重要起来。

sentences.en: The tensions between Catholicism and Protestantism.
sentences.zh: 天主教和新教之间的紧张关系。

sentences.en: And as a Protestant state starts to emerge in England, Wales is seen as like a threat.
sentences.zh: 随着英格兰开始出现一个新教国家，威尔士被视为一种威胁。

sentences.en: You know, we can't have these irregularities.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们不能有这些不规范的情况。

sentences.en: And what we can't have as well is the danger of a Catholic invasion coming to England via Wales from Ireland.
sentences.zh: 我们也不能容忍天主教通过爱尔兰经由威尔士入侵英格兰的危险。

sentences.en: And of course, that's how Henry took the throne of England in the first place.
sentences.zh: 当然，亨利起初就是这样夺取英格兰王位的。

sentences.en: He invaded England via Wales.
sentences.zh: 他经由威尔士入侵了英格兰。

sentences.en: So there is an attempt to kind of keep the Welsh on side to sort of, you know, to give more rights to their gentry, to iron out this complicated administrative situation.
sentences.zh: 所以有人试图让威尔士人站在自己这一边，你知道，给予他们的绅士更多权利，以理顺这种复杂的行政状况。

sentences.en: And Cromwell, you know, was a great fan of doing things, opriocracy in many ways.
sentences.zh: 而克伦威尔，你知道，在很多方面都是那种实干家。

sentences.en: Making omelettes by cracking eggs.
sentences.zh: 不打破鸡蛋就做不成煎蛋卷。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And now the Acts of Union is seen as kind of this moment of colonialism where Wales is essentially abolished as a separate political unit.
sentences.zh: 现在《联合法案》被视为一种殖民主义时刻，威尔士作为一个独立的政治单位基本上被废除了。

sentences.en: Whereas the reality of the 16th century was it was way more complicated than that.
sentences.zh: 然而16世纪的现实要复杂得多。

sentences.en: It wasn't some attempt to say Wales no longer exists.
sentences.zh: 这并不是要说威尔士不再存在。

sentences.en: There's no attempt to ban the Welsh language or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 没有任何试图禁止威尔士语之类的企图。

sentences.en: But well, quite the contrary, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但恰恰相反，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because the Bible is translated into Welsh.
sentences.zh: 因为《圣经》被翻译成了威尔士语。

sentences.en: So that's a hugely significant development.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个极其重要的发展。

sentences.en: And also Wales now gets representation in Parliament.
sentences.zh: 而且威尔士现在在议会中也有了代表。

sentences.en: It does get representation in Parliament.
sentences.zh: 它确实在议会中有了代表。

sentences.en: And that's symbolically important, more than practically important, perhaps, because, of course, there are a minority of the MPs at Westminster.
sentences.zh: 这在象征意义上比在实际意义上更重要，也许吧，因为当然，他们在威斯敏斯特的议员只是少数。

sentences.en: And just as today, you know, Welsh voices in Westminster are easily drowned out by English voices.
sentences.zh: 就像今天一样，你知道，威斯敏斯特的威尔士声音很容易被英国人的声音淹没。

sentences.en: You know, the whole question of the United Kingdom, whether we're talking about this period or today, is the size of England compared to the other constituent nations.
sentences.zh: 你知道，整个联合王国的问题，无论我们是在谈论这个时期还是今天，都是英格兰相对于其他组成国家的规模问题。

sentences.en: You know, English voices will always dominate the conversation.
sentences.zh: 你知道，英国人的声音总是会主导对话。

sentences.en: So Wales does get some representation through the Acts of Union.
sentences.zh: 所以威尔士确实通过《联合法案》获得了一些代表权。

sentences.en: But as you said, the translation of the Bible, you know, which happens a little after the Acts of Union, that's the really important moment, I think, in this period.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，《圣经》的翻译，你知道，发生在《联合法案》之后不久，我认为那是这个时期真正重要的时刻。

sentences.en: And that's done, you know,
sentences.zh: 那是，你知道，

sentences.en: with the approval of the English state as a way of ensuring that Wales joins this Protestant revolution and isn't some kind of Catholic outlier on England's doorstep.
sentences.zh: 在英国政府的批准下完成的，作为一种确保威尔士加入这场新教革命，而不是成为英格兰家门口的某种天主教异类的方式。

sentences.en: But what it does is give the Welsh language dignity and respect.
sentences.zh: 但它所做的是赋予了威尔士语尊严和尊重。

sentences.en: If you can hear the word of God in Welsh, if you can pray to God in Welsh, if you can be married in Welsh, you know, these are major things in people's lives.
sentences.zh: 如果你能用威尔士语听到上帝的话语，如果你能用威尔士语向上帝祈祷，如果你能用威尔士语结婚，你知道，这些都是人们生活中的大事。

sentences.en: And I think today we forget the importance of religion in past societies.
sentences.zh: 我认为今天我们忘记了宗教在过去社会中的重要性。

sentences.en: Not here.
sentences.zh: 在这里不是。

sentences.en: The word of God was everything.
sentences.zh: 上帝的话语就是一切。

sentences.en: And the fact that it's available in Welsh gives the Welsh language status and dignity.
sentences.zh: 它能以威尔士语呈现，赋予了威尔士语地位和尊严。

sentences.en: In a world where English was the language of law, it was the language of power, it was the language of politics, English was the language you needed to get on.
sentences.zh: 在一个英语是法律语言、权力语言、政治语言的世界里，英语是你想要出人头地所必需的语言。

sentences.en: And that meant it was very easy to portray Welsh as a backwards and civilised language.
sentences.zh: 这意味着很容易将威尔士语描绘成一种落后和未开化的语言。

sentences.en: And that did happen a lot.
sentences.zh: 这种情况确实发生了很多。

sentences.en: But a language can't be uncivilised if the word of God is written in that language.
sentences.zh: 但如果上帝的话语是用这种语言写成的，那么这种语言就不可能是未开化的。

sentences.en: And so the vast, vast majority of people in Wales are speaking Welsh throughout the 16th century, throughout the 17th century.
sentences.zh: 因此，在整个16世纪和17世纪，威尔士绝大多数人都在说威尔士语。

sentences.en: And then with the 18th century, with the development of industrialisation, then things do start to change.
sentences.zh: 然后到了18世纪，随着工业化的发展，情况确实开始发生变化。

sentences.en: And perhaps we could take a break at this point.
sentences.zh: 也许我们可以在这一点上休息一下。

sentences.en: And when we can come back, we could look at the coming of the Industrial Revolution to Wales and the impact that that has.
sentences.zh: 等我们回来，我们可以看看工业革命对威尔士的到来及其产生的影响。

sentences.en: Look at what these bastards have done to Wales.
sentences.zh: 看看这些混蛋对威尔士做了什么。

sentences.en: They've taken our coal, our water, our steel.
sentences.zh: 他们拿走了我们的煤炭、我们的水、我们的钢铁。

sentences.en: They buy our houses and live in them for a fortnight every year.
sentences.zh: 他们买下我们的房子，每年住上两周。

sentences.en: And what have they given us?
sentences.zh: 他们给了我们什么？

sentences.en: Absolutely nothing.
sentences.zh: 什么都没有。

sentences.en: We've been exploited, raped, controlled and punished by the English.
sentences.zh: 我们被英国人剥削、强奸、控制和惩罚。

sentences.en: And that is who we are playing this afternoon.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们今天下午要对阵的对手。

sentences.en: So that's the late Phil Bennett, the great Welsh rugby fly half in March 1977,
sentences.zh: 所以那是已故的菲尔·贝内特（Phil Bennett），伟大的威尔士橄榄球传接锋，在1977年3月，

sentences.en: before a Five Nations match, which Wales won 49.
sentences.zh: 在五国赛之前，威尔士赢了49分。

sentences.en: And yet, as I imagine you will know, Martin, the irony of that is that just a few weeks later,
sentences.zh: 然而，我想你一定知道，马丁，讽刺的是，仅仅几周后，

sentences.en: Phil Bennett and a lot of his teammates joined up with the English to go on the British Lions tour of New Zealand.
sentences.zh: 菲尔·贝内特和他的许多队友就加入了英国队，参加了不列颠雄狮队对新西兰的巡回赛。

sentences.en: So that moment actually speaks to exactly what you're writing about, which is the complicated relationship between Wales and England.
sentences.zh: 所以那一刻实际上准确地说明了你正在写的内容，即威尔士和英格兰之间复杂的关系。

sentences.en: So that quotation from Phil Bennett, which I could see you smirking while I started to read it, because it's very famous in Wales, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以菲尔·贝内特的那段引语，我看到我开始读的时候你在偷笑，因为它在威尔士非常有名，不是吗？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: He mentions coal, he mentions water, and he mentions steel.
sentences.zh: 他提到了煤炭，提到了水，还提到了钢铁。

sentences.en: So we've cantered through the medieval period.
sentences.zh: 所以我们已经快速浏览了中世纪。

sentences.en: We skipped over a little bit of the early modern.
sentences.zh: 我们跳过了一点近代早期。

sentences.en: And as we approach the 18th and 19th centuries,
sentences.zh: 当我们接近18和19世纪时，

sentences.en: obviously coal and steel transform Wales, don't they?
sentences.zh: 显然煤炭和钢铁改变了威尔士，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, just explain, I guess, to the listeners, because previously Wales had been very, very rural.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想请你向听众解释一下，因为在此之前威尔士一直非常、非常农村化。

sentences.en: And then with the Industrial Revolution, it has completely changed.
sentences.zh: 然后随着工业革命，它彻底改变了。

sentences.en: Yeah, if you go back to the middle of the 18th century, Wales is a rural backwater in many ways.
sentences.zh: 是的，如果你回到18世纪中期，威尔士在许多方面都是一个农村落后地区。

sentences.en: It's isolated, it's marginalised, probably at least 90% of the population only speak Welsh.
sentences.zh: 它与世隔绝，被边缘化，可能至少90%的人口只说威尔士语。

sentences.en: Some of the gentry are kind of moving to England and have connections.
sentences.zh: 一些绅士开始搬到英格兰并建立联系。

sentences.en: But by and large, Wales is on the periphery of the United Kingdom and economically just not that important.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，威尔士处于联合王国的边缘，在经济上并不那么重要。

sentences.en: But the Industrial Revolution changes everything because Wales has the right minerals.
sentences.zh: 但工业革命改变了一切，因为威尔士拥有合适的矿产。

sentences.en: It has coal in abundance and not just coal, it has very good quality coal, but it also has the minerals you need to make iron and later on steel.
sentences.zh: 它拥有丰富的煤炭，而且不仅是煤炭，还有非常优质的煤炭，但它也拥有制造铁和后来制造钢铁所需的矿产。

sentences.en: And that changes Wales because suddenly it matters within the United Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 这改变了威尔士，因为它突然在联合王国中变得重要起来。

sentences.en: The British government becomes more interested in Wales.
sentences.zh: 英国政府开始对威尔士产生更多兴趣。

sentences.en: It becomes interested in why do they not speak English there?
sentences.zh: 它开始对为什么那里的人不说英语产生兴趣。

sentences.en: And that question is asked because it doesn't seem to make sense to the English state, because to them, English is the language of modernity and progress, etc.
sentences.zh: 这个问题之所以被提出，是因为对英国政府来说这似乎说不通，因为对他们来说，英语是现代性和进步等的语言。

sentences.en: So how come a corner of our kingdom doesn't speak this language?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么我们王国的一个角落不说这种语言呢？

sentences.en: And because industrialisation creates very difficult living conditions,
sentences.zh: 而且因为工业化创造了非常困难的生活条件，

sentences.en: you know, working in coal industry or the iron industry was not a pleasant experience.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在煤炭工业或钢铁工业工作并不是一种愉快的经历。

sentences.en: Yes, the wages were better than living off the land, but the living conditions were very difficult as towns grew up very fast,
sentences.zh: 是的，工资比靠土地生活要好，但随着城镇迅速发展，生活条件非常困难，

sentences.en: you know, full of disease, full of overcrowding, etc., etc.
sentences.zh: 你知道，充满了疾病，充满了拥挤等等等等。

sentences.en: So Wales starts to develop a reputation for being unruly.
sentences.zh: 所以威尔士开始以难以管教而闻名。

sentences.en: There are a series of kind of riots and protests.
sentences.zh: 发生了一系列骚乱和抗议活动。

sentences.en: The army is sent in on several occasions and opens fire and kills people.
sentences.zh: 军队多次被派往那里，开火并杀害了民众。

sentences.en: And as the English government is saying, well, what are we going to do about this?
sentences.zh: 当英国政府说，好吧，我们对此该怎么办？

sentences.en: Attention starts to focus on the Welsh language.
sentences.zh: 注意力开始集中在威尔士语上。

sentences.en: And the idea that maybe the problem is that the Welsh people don't speak the same language as the rest of us.
sentences.zh: 以及认为问题可能在于威尔士人不说我们其他人所说的同一种语言。

sentences.en: And maybe we need to do something about that.
sentences.zh: 也许我们需要对此采取一些行动。

sentences.en: And that turns people's attention to the question of education.
sentences.zh: 这让人们开始关注教育问题。

sentences.en: And MPs are saying, you know, it's cheaper to send some schoolmasters to Wales than to hold, you know, a unit of army there.
sentences.zh: 议员们说，你知道，派一些校监去威尔士比在那里驻扎一支军队要便宜得多。

sentences.en: Just before we come to education, because this is obviously such a massive thing,
sentences.zh: 在我们谈到教育之前，因为这显然是一件大事，

sentences.en: just on the Industrial Revolution and the coal and the steel and the huge development of the South Wales Valleys and so on.
sentences.zh: 就工业革命、煤炭、钢铁以及南威尔士山谷的巨大发展等等而言。

sentences.en: I mean, obviously, one thing that that does is it creates a great disparity between North and South Wales in a much more marked way than existed before.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，显然，这样做的一件事是造成了北威尔士和南威尔士之间巨大的差异，这种差异比以前更加显著。

sentences.en: But there are some historians, aren't there, who say, well, this is basically a purely extractive economy.
sentences.zh: 但也有一些历史学家认为，这基本上是一个纯粹的掠夺性经济。

sentences.en: So this really is a colonial economy.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实是一个殖民经济。

sentences.en: The English are doing to the Welsh what they're doing to so many people around the world.
sentences.zh: 英国人对威尔士人所做的事情，正是他们对世界各地许多人所做的事情。

sentences.en: They're just taking their resources and Wales is gaining nothing from this.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在掠夺资源，而威尔士从中一无所获。

sentences.en: Is that true?
sentences.zh: 这是真的吗？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, it is literally an extractive economy because things have been dug out of the ground and sent to other places.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，这确实是一个掠夺性经济，因为东西是从地下挖出来并送到其他地方的。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It's a complicated one because there isn't a straightforward pattern.
sentences.zh: 这是一个复杂的问题，因为没有一个简单的模式。

sentences.en: Some of the industrialists are English.
sentences.zh: 一些实业家是英国人。

sentences.en: You know, some of the early ironmasters are English, but they settle in Wales.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一些早期的铁器大亨是英国人，但他们在威尔士定居。

sentences.en: They become part of Welsh society.
sentences.zh: 他们成为了威尔士社会的一部分。

sentences.en: You know, some of them learn Welsh.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们中有些人学会了威尔士语。

sentences.en: So, you know, it's a little bit misleading, I think, to call them English.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为称他们为英国人有点误导。

sentences.en: In the coal industry, a lot of the big early developments are led by local entrepreneurs, you know, making money, looking for opportunities to make money.
sentences.zh: 在煤炭工业中，许多早期的重大发展是由当地企业家领导的，你知道，他们赚钱，寻找赚钱的机会。

sentences.en: Yes, there are English coal owners, but the majority are Welsh.
sentences.zh: 是的，有英国煤矿主，但大多数是威尔士人。

sentences.en: And of course, it's not always easy to distinguish between who is English and Welsh because you have families with Welsh backgrounds living in England.
sentences.zh: 当然，区分谁是英国人谁是威尔士人并不总是那么容易，因为有些家庭有威尔士背景却住在英格兰。

sentences.en: You have English families who settle in Wales.
sentences.zh: 也有在威尔士定居的英国家庭。

sentences.en: Where there is some extraction that's going on in many ways is in the mineral rights.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，确实存在某种掠夺，那就是矿产开采权。

sentences.en: So if you were the local landowner, you were entitled to a share of the profits, essentially, when somebody dug things out of your ground.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是当地的地主，当有人从你的土地上挖掘东西时，你基本上有权分享利润。

sentences.en: And a lot of the landowners, people like the Marquesses of Butte, were not local.
sentences.zh: 而且很多地主，像比特侯爵那样的人，并不是当地人。

sentences.en: And money is leaving Wales to go to England via the mineral rights.
sentences.zh: 钱通过矿产开采权从威尔士流向了英格兰。

sentences.en: So industrialisation creates immense wealth.
sentences.zh: 所以工业化创造了巨大的财富。

sentences.en: But just as in England, that wealth is very concentrated in a handful of pockets.
sentences.zh: 但就像在英格兰一样，这些财富非常集中在少数人的口袋里。

sentences.en: You know, in many ways, this is a story of class oppression rather than national oppression.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在很多方面，这是一个阶级压迫的故事，而不是民族压迫的故事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I wanted to ask you about that.
sentences.zh: 所以我正想问你这个问题。

sentences.en: Wales is historically very much a Labour voting country.
sentences.zh: 威尔士在历史上是一个非常支持工党的国家。

sentences.en: And presumably the roots of that lie in the Industrial Revolution and the dilution of the sense that what is the principal differences between English and Welsh comes to be blurred.
sentences.zh: 据推测，其根源在于工业革命，以及那种认为英格兰人和威尔士人之间存在主要差异的观念被淡化了。

sentences.en: And it comes to be between the industrial masses and those who are profiting from their labour.
sentences.zh: 这种差异逐渐变成了工业大众与那些从他们劳动中获利的人之间的差异。

sentences.en: I mean, in the 19th century, Wales is a liberal country.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在19世纪，威尔士是一个自由主义国家。

sentences.en: You know, Wales is voting liberal.
sentences.zh: 你知道，威尔士投票支持自由党。

sentences.en: I mean, of course, it's not a full democracy in that period.
sentences.zh: 当然，那个时期还不是完全的民主。

sentences.en: But the Liberal Party see themselves as a symbol of Welshness.
sentences.zh: 但自由党将自己视为威尔士身份的象征。

sentences.en: They promote the rights of nonconformity.
sentences.zh: 他们促进非国教徒的权利。

sentences.en: And Wales was a chapel-going society.
sentences.zh: 而威尔士是一个信奉礼拜堂的社会。

sentences.en: And that was a symbol of difference with England.
sentences.zh: 那是与英格兰不同的象征。

sentences.en: The Liberal Party celebrate Welsh culture, Welsh language, Welsh history.
sentences.zh: 自由党推崇威尔士文化、威尔士语言和威尔士历史。

sentences.en: You know, there is this middle class liberal establishment who are very much pushing a Welsh agenda, celebrating Welsh nationhood.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有这样一个中产阶级自由派建制派，他们非常积极地推动威尔士议程，颂扬威尔士民族性。

sentences.en: I mean, some historians talk about Wales being reborn in the late 19th century.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，一些历史学家谈到威尔士在19世纪末重生。

sentences.en: It rediscovers its history.
sentences.zh: 它重新发现了自己的历史。

sentences.en: It rediscovers its sense of identity.
sentences.zh: 它重新发现了自己的身份认同感。

sentences.en: And that's part, of course, the European movement.
sentences.zh: 当然，这也是欧洲运动的一部分。

sentences.en: You know, across Europe in the late 19th century, there are national movements and Wales is part of that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在19世纪末的整个欧洲，都有民族运动，而威尔士也是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: And Wales is presumably very, very well suited to that because there really is a properly ancient Bardic tradition.
sentences.zh: 而且威尔士大概非常适合这一点，因为那里确实有非常古老的吟游诗人传统。

sentences.en: And scope for dressing up as Druids is very, very rich and exciting.
sentences.zh: 而且装扮成德鲁伊的空间非常丰富且令人兴奋。

sentences.en: I mean, some of the traditions are invented.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有些传统是发明出来的。

sentences.en: Yeah, but that's what romantic nationalism is all about, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是的，但这就是浪漫民族主义的本质，不是吗？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: But they're drawing upon something real.
sentences.zh: 但他们借鉴的是真实的东西。

sentences.en: Welshness isn't invented.
sentences.zh: 威尔士身份并非凭空捏造。

sentences.en: You know, the sense of history, the sense of difference to England is very profound because there was a real cultural difference.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这种历史感，这种与英格兰不同的感觉非常深刻，因为确实存在真正的文化差异。

sentences.en: You know, even at the end of the 19th century, you know, half the population of Wales speak a different language to England.
sentences.zh: 你知道，即使在19世纪末，威尔士一半的人口说的语言也与英格兰不同。

sentences.en: That's not that long ago.
sentences.zh: 那并没有过去太久。

sentences.en: So that's a massive thing, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以这是一件大事，不是吗？

sentences.en: The issue of the language and education.
sentences.zh: 语言和教育问题。

sentences.en: So here's the sort of standard version, I guess, that I had read before I read your book.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我读你的书之前读到的标准版本。

sentences.en: And I guess a lot of people in Wales will tell you, which is that in the middle of the 19th century, the 1840s, Westminster, the directive comes down, stamp out Welsh.
sentences.zh: 我想威尔士的很多人都会告诉你，那就是在19世纪中叶，即1840年代，威斯敏斯特下达了指令，要铲除威尔士语。

sentences.en: Welsh, everybody should learn English.
sentences.zh: 威尔士语，每个人都应该学习英语。

sentences.en: Welsh is backward and primitive.
sentences.zh: 威尔士语是落后和原始的。

sentences.en: And what the famous sort of embodiment of this is this thing that you have to wear around your neck at school called the Welsh knot.
sentences.zh: 而这种观念最著名的体现就是你在学校里必须戴在脖子上的东西，叫做“威尔士结”。

sentences.en: And if you're caught speaking Welsh, you put it on.
sentences.zh: 如果你被抓到说威尔士语，你就得戴上它。

sentences.en: And then the boy who's, or I guess girl, who's wearing it at the end of the day is punished in some way.
sentences.zh: 然后那个戴着它的男孩，或者我想是女孩，在一天结束时会受到某种惩罚。

sentences.en: And people are beaten for speaking Welsh.
sentences.zh: 人们因为说威尔士语而挨打。

sentences.en: I mean, I can remember.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我记得。

sentences.en: So my grandfather was Welsh.
sentences.zh: 我的祖父是威尔士人。

sentences.en: Welsh, he had emigrated from Wales, as so many people did, in the sort of early year or middle of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 威尔士人，他从威尔士移民了，就像许多人一样，在20世纪初或中期。

sentences.en: He'd lost his accent.
sentences.zh: 他已经失去了口音。

sentences.en: He was still very proud to be Welsh.
sentences.zh: 但他仍然为自己是威尔士人感到非常自豪。

sentences.en: And he would, I remember him saying to me when I was little, you know, we were beaten at school for speaking in Welsh.
sentences.zh: 我记得我小时候他对我讲过，你知道，我们在学校因为说威尔士语而挨打。

sentences.en: And I always, I mean, I have to say, he was a great teller of tall stories, which obviously does not run in the family at all.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，他是个很会讲离奇故事的人，这显然不是我们家族的遗传。

sentences.en: So I had my doubts even then.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时就有所怀疑。

sentences.en: But Martin, your book suggests that this is all a little bit exaggerated and oversimplified.
sentences.zh: 但是马丁，你的书表明这一切有点被夸大和过度简化了。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's complicated, the history.
sentences.zh: 是的，历史很复杂。

sentences.en: I mean, definitely in the middle of the 19th century, the British government was worried about Wales.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在19世纪中叶，英国政府确实担心威尔士。

sentences.en: And there is a sense that it is a threat in some ways.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，人们确实感觉到这是一种威胁。

sentences.en: And the language being the obvious sense of difference, that's where attention focuses.
sentences.zh: 语言是显而易见的差异感，这就是注意力集中的地方。

sentences.en: And commissioners are sent to Wales and they have this big education inquiry that says, you know, Welsh is a backwards language.
sentences.zh: 专员被派往威尔士，他们进行了大规模的教育调查，说威尔士语是一种落后的语言。

sentences.en: It's holding the Welsh back from joining civilisation.
sentences.zh: 它阻碍了威尔士人融入文明。

sentences.en: And the sooner the language sort of disappears, the better Wales will be.
sentences.zh: 威尔士语消失得越快，威尔士就会越好。

sentences.en: But actually, not a lot actually happens after that in terms of policy, because, you know, the early in the mid 19th century, the British state is very small.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，在那之后政策层面并没有发生太多事情，因为在19世纪初和中期，英国政府规模很小。

sentences.en: It's not actually doing an awful lot in terms of interfering in daily life in any sphere.
sentences.zh: 它实际上并没有在干预日常生活的任何领域做太多事情。

sentences.en: There are limited grants available in the education, you know, in the field of education.
sentences.zh: 在教育领域有有限的拨款。

sentences.en: But by and large, you know, this is a period of kind of laissez-faire politics.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，这是一个自由放任政治的时期。

sentences.en: The government is hands off.
sentences.zh: 政府是不干涉的。

sentences.en: So it has no respect for the Welsh language.
sentences.zh: 所以它对威尔士语没有尊重。

sentences.en: It certainly would be happier if the Welsh language died off.
sentences.zh: 如果威尔士语消亡，它肯定会更高兴。

sentences.en: But it doesn't really do anything about that.
sentences.zh: 但它并没有真正为此做任何事情。

sentences.en: But what does happen within Wales is that parents want their children to learn English, because English is the language of modernity, of law, of power.
sentences.zh: 但在威尔士内部发生的事情是，父母希望他们的孩子学习英语，因为英语是现代性、法律和权力的语言。

sentences.en: One chapel minister in North Wales says, you know, people look around and they see that anybody with a job that doesn't break your back speaks English.
sentences.zh: 北威尔士的一位礼拜堂牧师说，你知道，人们环顾四周，看到任何一份不累人的工作都需要说英语。

sentences.en: People understood that English was the route out of misery and poverty.
sentences.zh: 人们明白英语是摆脱苦难和贫困的途径。

sentences.en: And that meant schools, not out of some diktat from Westminster, but because of local pressures are run through the medium of English.
sentences.zh: 这意味着学校不是因为威斯敏斯特的某种指令，而是因为当地的压力，以英语为媒介进行教学。

sentences.en: They're there to teach people English.
sentences.zh: 它们的存在是为了教人们英语。

sentences.en: The question is, how do you teach people who don't speak a language a new language?
sentences.zh: 问题是，你如何教那些不说某种语言的人学习一门新语言？

sentences.en: And some people thought the way to do that was to basically beat them if they spoke their domestic language.
sentences.zh: 有些人认为这样做的方法基本上是如果他们说母语就打他们。

sentences.en: And the Welsh not, this wooden board put around people at children's necks if they were heard to speak Welsh.
sentences.zh: 还有“威尔士结”，如果孩子们被听到说威尔士语，就会被戴在脖子上。

sentences.en: You know, that was to almost create a sense of shame and association between speaking Welsh and shame and being humiliated.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那几乎是为了制造一种羞耻感，将说威尔士语与羞耻和被羞辱联系起来。

sentences.en: Do the parents back this?
sentences.zh: 父母支持这样做吗？

sentences.en: The parents do seem to back it.
sentences.zh: 父母似乎确实支持它。

sentences.en: There doesn't seem to be any kind of outcry against it.
sentences.zh: 似乎没有任何反对的声音。

sentences.en: And certainly there is some evidence that those kind of measures are introduced in some places at the request of parents.
sentences.zh: 而且确实有一些证据表明，这些措施是在一些地方应家长的要求引入的。

sentences.en: And most of the teachers in these areas are Welsh speakers.
sentences.zh: 而且这些地区的老师大多是威尔士语使用者。

sentences.en: You know, they're local people from the community.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们是来自社区的当地人。

sentences.en: This is something that the Welsh people are doing to themselves.
sentences.zh: 这是威尔士人对自己做的事情。

sentences.en: The government isn't telling them to, but the government agrees with the broad principle.
sentences.zh: 政府并没有告诉他们这样做，但政府同意这一大原则。

sentences.en: The problem is it didn't work.
sentences.zh: 问题是它没有奏效。

sentences.en: Because what was literally happening in these schools was these kids don't hear English outside the school because nobody's speaking it in the community.
sentences.zh: 因为在这些学校里发生的事情是，这些孩子在校外听不到英语，因为社区里没有人说英语。

sentences.en: You know, in rural Wales, these are entirely Welsh-speaking places.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在威尔士农村，这些地方完全是说威尔士语的。

sentences.en: So they're coming into school.
sentences.zh: 所以他们来到学校。

sentences.en: They've been taught to read these words through literally somebody putting them up on a blackboard or being given a book.
sentences.zh: 他们被教导通过有人把单词写在黑板上或给他们一本书来认读这些单词。

sentences.en: And the teacher says the word and the children repeat after them.
sentences.zh: 老师说出单词，孩子们跟着重复。

sentences.en: And they're learning how to say these words.
sentences.zh: 他们正在学习如何说这些单词。

sentences.en: They're learning how to kind of read.
sentences.zh: 他们正在学习如何阅读。

sentences.en: But because nobody is telling them what these words mean in their own language, they have no idea what they are reading.
sentences.zh: 但因为没有人告诉他们这些单词在他们自己的语言中是什么意思，他们根本不知道自己在读什么。

sentences.en: That's not Duolingo, is it?
sentences.zh: 那不是多邻国，对吧？

sentences.en: So in that case, what is it that leads to the decline of Welsh, which has been such a cause celebre in Wales in the 20th century?
sentences.zh: 那么在这种情况下，是什么导致了威尔士语的衰落，这在20世纪的威尔士一直是一个著名的争议焦点？

sentences.en: The key issue, I'd argue, is migration.
sentences.zh: 我认为关键问题是移民。

sentences.en: So industrialisation creates well-paid jobs.
sentences.zh: 工业化创造了高薪工作。

sentences.en: You know, they're harsh communities, overcrowded communities, et cetera, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那是艰苦的社区，过度拥挤的社区等等。

sentences.en: But ultimately, they are better paid jobs than living in the land.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，它们比靠土地生活的工作报酬更高。

sentences.en: So people start to move into industrial Wales from places like Shropshire, the southwest of England, and then further afield.
sentences.zh: 所以人们开始从什罗普郡、英格兰西南部以及更远的地方搬到工业化的威尔士。

sentences.en: And that brings the English language into working class communities for the first time in many ways.
sentences.zh: 这在很多方面第一次将英语带入了工人阶级社区。

sentences.en: Now, initially, those early migrants learn Welsh because that's the dominant language of the community.
sentences.zh: 起初，那些早期的移民学习威尔士语，因为那是社区的主要语言。

sentences.en: But as their numbers grow, they stop learning Welsh.
sentences.zh: 但随着他们人数的增加，他们停止学习威尔士语。

sentences.en: And increasingly, local people start learning English.
sentences.zh: 而且越来越多的人开始学习英语。

sentences.en: And because they are starting to learn English at school, particularly after people start working out the Welsh knot doesn't work,
sentences.zh: 因为他们开始在学校学习英语，特别是在人们发现“威尔士结”不起作用之后，

sentences.en: we actually need to teach them English through the medium of Welsh.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上需要通过威尔士语作为媒介来教他们英语。

sentences.en: As schooling, as education policies get better, people are learning English at school, and then they're using English in the community with these migrants.
sentences.zh: 随着学校教育和教育政策的改善，人们在学校学习英语，然后在社区里与这些移民使用英语。

sentences.en: And as migration grows, the balance, the linguistic balance in industrial communities starts to tip.
sentences.zh: 随着移民的增加，工业社区的语言平衡开始倾斜。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You've got some amazing stats here.
sentences.zh: 你这里有一些惊人的统计数据。

sentences.en: You've got, so the Rhonda saw its population grow from under 1,000 in 1851 to more than 150,000 by 1911.
sentences.zh: 你提到，朗达的人口从1851年的不到1000人增长到1911年的超过15万人。

sentences.en: And you talk about the growth of Cardiff, which had been a small market town and ends up one of the,
sentences.zh: 你谈到了卡迪夫的发展，它曾经是一个小集镇，最终成为了，

sentences.en: I mean, not just one of the most kind of important industrial ports, but one of the most cosmopolitan.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不仅是最重要的工业港口之一，而且是最国际化的港口之一。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, industry brings people from, you know, from all over the world.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，工业带来了来自世界各地的人。

sentences.en: And Cardiff has, you know, in some ways, the oldest black community anywhere in the United Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 卡迪夫在某些方面拥有英国任何地方最古老的黑人社区。

sentences.en: It's very self-contained in the docks area of Cardiff, which are a little bit separated from the main city.
sentences.zh: 它在卡迪夫的码头区非常自成一体，与主城区稍微有点分离。

sentences.en: It's often treated appallingly by the local authorities.
sentences.zh: 它经常受到地方当局的恶劣对待。

sentences.en: There's considerable racism.
sentences.zh: 存在相当严重的种族主义。

sentences.en: But industrialization does change the very structure of Welsh society.
sentences.zh: 但工业化确实改变了威尔士社会的结构。

sentences.en: And one other thing that, as well as the English language arriving, there's an English game, which the Welsh adopt as their own.
sentences.zh: 除了英语的到来，还有一项英国运动，威尔士人将其采纳为自己的运动。

sentences.en: And I'm curious why this and how this happens.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇为什么会这样，以及这是如何发生的。

sentences.en: And that game is, of course, rugby, which is now absolutely identified with Wales.
sentences.zh: 那项运动当然就是橄榄球，现在它已经完全与威尔士画上了等号。

sentences.en: I mean, Wales are obviously at the Football World Cup, which is why we're doing this story.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，威尔士显然打进了足球世界杯，这就是我们做这个专题的原因。

sentences.en: But really, rugby has always been Wales' traditional game.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，橄榄球一直是威尔士的传统运动。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: It's a sport of the English public schools.
sentences.zh: 这是英国公立学校的运动。

sentences.en: And some of the Welsh gentry, some of the Welsh middle classes, are being sent to English public schools and are coming back with this game.
sentences.zh: 一些威尔士绅士和中产阶级被送往英国公立学校，回来时就带回了这项运动。

sentences.en: But also because it was the sport of the English public schools, it had some social status.
sentences.zh: 而且因为它曾是英国公立学校的运动，所以它具有一定的社会地位。

sentences.en: And, you know, when we think about why individuals decided to speak to their children in English rather than Welsh, it was because English had social status.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我们思考为什么人们决定用英语而不是威尔士语与孩子交流时，是因为英语具有社会地位。

sentences.en: And it's the same with, you know, with anything that's coming from England.
sentences.zh: 任何来自英格兰的事物都是如此。

sentences.en: There's some cachet to it.
sentences.zh: 它带有一种光环。
