sentences.en: So people adopt rugby because of that.
sentences.zh: 所以人们因为这一点而接受了橄榄球。

sentences.en: The sport spreads very quickly, but it very quickly becomes a symbol of Welshness.
sentences.zh: 这项运动传播得非常快，但很快就成为了威尔士身份的象征。

sentences.en: Because you have these diverse communities in industrial areas where people have come from all over the place, rugby enabled them to unite under kind of the banner of Welshness.
sentences.zh: 因为在工业区有各种各样的群体，人们来自四面八方，橄榄球使他们能够在威尔士精神的旗帜下团结起来。

sentences.en: It didn't matter if you're middle class or working class, whether you spoke English or Welsh.
sentences.zh: 无论你是中产阶级还是工人阶级，无论你说英语还是威尔士语，这都不重要。

sentences.en: It didn't matter what your family heritage were.
sentences.zh: 你的家庭背景是什么也不重要。

sentences.en: And lots of the early Welsh rugby players are migrants from England, but they have moved to Wales.
sentences.zh: 许多早期的威尔士橄榄球运动员是从英格兰移民过来的，但他们搬到了威尔士。

sentences.en: So they don the Welsh, the red shirt.
sentences.zh: 所以他们穿上了威尔士的红色球衣。

sentences.en: And because Wales ends up with a very good rugby team in the late 19th century, in the early 20th century, that adds an emotional element to it because you don't want your national
sentences.zh: 而且因为威尔士在19世纪末、20世纪初拥有一支非常出色的橄榄球队，这增加了一种情感因素，因为你不会希望你的国家

sentences.en: symbols to be something that you're bad at.
sentences.zh: 象征是你表现糟糕的东西。

sentences.en: And because Wales happens to have a really good team, it becomes incredibly attractive.
sentences.zh: 正因为威尔士恰好拥有一支非常棒的球队，它变得极具吸引力。

sentences.en: So rugby becomes a really powerful symbol of Welshness, which unifies people in a way that kind of language or politics doesn't.
sentences.zh: 所以橄榄球成为了威尔士精神的一种强大象征，它以语言或政治无法做到的方式团结了人们。

sentences.en: And I'd argue that through the 20th century, the fact that Wales had its own national teams
sentences.zh: 我认为在整个20世纪，威尔士拥有自己的国家队

sentences.en: in football and rugby is one of the key reasons why Welsh identity has stayed so powerful.
sentences.zh: （足球和橄榄球）是威尔士身份保持如此强大的关键原因之一。

sentences.en: Well, I wanted to ask about that because, I mean, there's so much we will have to skip over.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想问问这一点，因为我们不得不跳过很多内容。

sentences.en: So there's obviously a Welsh prime minister, a Welsh speaker in David Lloyd George.
sentences.zh: 显然有一位威尔士首相，一位讲威尔士语的戴维·劳合·乔治。

sentences.en: As you say, Wales has become economically transformed in the previous hundred years.
sentences.zh: 如你所说，威尔士在过去一百年里经济发生了转型。

sentences.en: And I suppose one thing that you might not have been able to predict at that point was the revival of Welsh nationalism.
sentences.zh: 我想当时你可能无法预料到的一件事是威尔士民族主义的复兴。

sentences.en: So Plaid Cymru, the Welsh Nationalist Party, is founded in 1925.
sentences.zh: 威尔士民族党（Plaid Cymru）成立于1925年。

sentences.en: Do you think the rise of Welsh nationalism was inevitable because it has 19th century roots?
sentences.zh: 你认为威尔士民族主义的兴起是不可避免的吗，因为它有19世纪的根源？

sentences.en: It happens all over Europe, nationalist parties and so on.
sentences.zh: 这种情况在欧洲各地都有发生，民族主义政党等等。

sentences.en: Or do you think it is a distinctive story because obviously that economy in which Wales has built its new identity is doomed, actually.
sentences.zh: 还是你认为这是一个独特的案例，因为显然威尔士建立新身份所依赖的经济基础实际上已经注定要失败了。

sentences.en: It's quite a short-lived moment, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常短暂的时期，不是吗？

sentences.en: The industrial golden age, because as you say in your book, the interwar years are dreadful for Wales.
sentences.zh: 工业黄金时代，因为正如你在书中所说，两次世界大战之间的岁月对威尔士来说是可怕的。

sentences.en: And then after that, it's kind of downhill for coal and steel and all these things.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，煤炭、钢铁以及所有这些产业都走下坡路了。

sentences.en: Something must be done.
sentences.zh: 必须采取行动。

sentences.en: The future Edward VIII, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 未来的爱德华八世，对吧？

sentences.en: Visiting the depressed areas.
sentences.zh: 去视察那些萧条地区。

sentences.en: So is nationalism a reaction to that?
sentences.zh: 那么民族主义是对这种情况的反应吗？

sentences.en: Or is it more just an inevitable, like Irish nationalism, a product of that sort of swirl of 19th century ideas?
sentences.zh: 还是说它更像爱尔兰民族主义一样，是19世纪那种思想浪潮的必然产物？

sentences.en: The important thing to remember about Welsh nationalism in the early 20th century is that it's not political, it's cultural.
sentences.zh: 关于20世纪初的威尔士民族主义，要记住重要的一点是，它不是政治性的，而是文化性的。

sentences.en: The goal is not necessarily an independent Wales.
sentences.zh: 目标不一定是独立的威尔士。

sentences.en: The goal is protecting the Welsh language.
sentences.zh: 目标是保护威尔士语。

sentences.en: And because the Welsh language was so clearly in decline by the 1920s and the 1930s, partly because of these demographic changes we've already talked about, but also in the 20s and
sentences.zh: 因为到20世纪20年代和30年代，威尔士语显然在衰落，部分原因是由于我们已经讨论过的人口结构变化，而且在20和

sentences.en: 30s, there's a mass migration from Wales because of the Depression.
sentences.zh: 30年代，由于大萧条，威尔士出现了大规模移民。

sentences.en: And by the 20s and 30s, people are starting to think the Welsh language might actually die out in the next century.
sentences.zh: 到了20和30年代，人们开始认为威尔士语可能真的会在下个世纪消亡。

sentences.en: And unless we act, nothing is going to, you know, that's actually going to happen.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不采取行动，什么都不会发生，你知道，这真的会发生。

sentences.en: So, you know, the initial kind of birth of Plaid Cymru and the first couple of decades of Welsh nationalism, it's not about politics.
sentences.zh: 所以，威尔士民族党的最初诞生和威尔士民族主义的前几十年，并不是关于政治的。

sentences.en: It's not about trying to rebuild the Welsh economy.
sentences.zh: 不是关于试图重建威尔士经济的。

sentences.en: It's about trying to protect the language.
sentences.zh: 而是关于试图保护语言的。

sentences.en: And indeed, in the early period of Plaid Cymru, there's actually an antipathy towards industry.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在威尔士民族党的早期，甚至对工业有一种反感。

sentences.en: And there's some people saying, actually, the future for Wales should be if we go backwards
sentences.zh: 有些人说，威尔士的未来应该是倒退

sentences.en: and we become another rural agricultural society again, because that's when Welsh was at its strongeSt.
sentences.zh: 回到另一个农村农业社会，因为那是威尔士语最强大的时候。

sentences.en: It's only in the post-1945 period does Welsh nationalism start to develop this political edge and people start to really kind of debate, what is our relationship with Westminster?
sentences.zh: 直到1945年后，威尔士民族主义才开始发展出这种政治色彩，人们开始真正辩论：我们与威斯敏斯特的关系是什么？

sentences.en: Should we have our own parliament?
sentences.zh: 我们应该有自己的议会吗？

sentences.en: Should we be an independent nation?
sentences.zh: 我们应该成为一个独立的国家吗？

sentences.en: And so what is the state of play now with, in terms of that, in terms of Wales' sense of itself in relation to England and in relation to the idea of Britain?
sentences.zh: 那么，就威尔士相对于英格兰以及相对于英国概念的自我认知而言，现在的状况如何？

sentences.en: So, well, Wales has retained a very strong sense of itself.
sentences.zh: 嗯，威尔士保留了非常强烈的自我意识。

sentences.en: Despite the paranoia in some ways, you know, of the early 20th century, Welshness did survive.
sentences.zh: 尽管20世纪初在某些方面存在偏执，但威尔士精神确实存活了下来。

sentences.en: The Welsh language was weakened, but Welshness itself survived because it wasn't just based upon the language.
sentences.zh: 威尔士语被削弱了，但威尔士精神本身存活了下来，因为它不仅仅基于语言。

sentences.en: And as I said, sport is one of the reasons why I think that happened.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，我认为体育是这种情况发生的原因之一。

sentences.en: So Welshness has continued to live on.
sentences.zh: 所以威尔士精神继续存在。

sentences.en: But the question is, what does it mean?
sentences.zh: 但问题是，这意味着什么？

sentences.en: Should it have a political role?
sentences.zh: 它应该有政治角色吗？

sentences.en: And increasingly, in the second half of the 20th century, as successive governments in
sentences.zh: 在20世纪下半叶，随着威斯敏斯特历届政府

sentences.en: Westminster failed to deal with the economic problems of Wales, increasing numbers of people
sentences.zh: 未能解决威尔士的经济问题，越来越多的人

sentences.en: started to say, the only way to rebuild our economy is to take matters into our own hands.
sentences.zh: 开始说，重建我们经济的唯一方法就是把命运掌握在自己手中。

sentences.en: It's a minority throughout the period.
sentences.zh: 在整个时期内，这都是少数派。

sentences.en: And even today, opinion polls suggest, you know, maybe only a quarter of the population support Welsh independence.
sentences.zh: 即使在今天，民意调查也显示，可能只有四分之一的人口支持威尔士独立。

sentences.en: But it is growing.
sentences.zh: 但它正在增长。

sentences.en: Part of the story there is Brexit, because the United Kingdom that people used to have an emotional connection to doesn't exist in many ways.
sentences.zh: 其中的部分原因是英国脱欧，因为人们曾经与之有情感联系的联合王国在许多方面已经不复存在了。

sentences.en: Though Wales, a majority in Wales voted for Brexit.
sentences.zh: 尽管威尔士，威尔士的大多数人投票支持脱欧。

sentences.en: They did, but not necessarily because they wanted to break away from the European Union, but because
sentences.zh: 他们确实投了，但不一定是因为他们想脱离欧盟，而是因为

sentences.en: it was sticking two fingers up at the establishment, an establishment that had let them down.
sentences.zh: 这是在向建制派竖中指，一个让他们失望的建制派。

sentences.en: And I think it was really a vote against the establishment rather than a vote for, you know, the nuances of Brexit.
sentences.zh: 我认为这确实是对建制派的投票，而不是对脱欧细微差别的投票。

sentences.en: But what Brexit also showed was that major constitutional change can happen.
sentences.zh: 但脱欧也表明，重大的宪法变革是可以发生的。

sentences.en: You know, 10 years ago, people were saying, you know, Welsh independence is a pipe dream.
sentences.zh: 你知道，10年前，人们说威尔士独立是白日梦。

sentences.en: You know, it's not much more than 10 years ago that people were saying the idea that Britain would leave the EU.
sentences.zh: 你知道，距离人们说英国会脱欧的想法也不过10年多一点。

sentences.en: You know, that would have seen fantastical politics.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那在当时会被视为异想天开的政治。

sentences.en: Rapid change can happen.
sentences.zh: 快速的变革是可以发生的。

sentences.en: Major constitutional change can happen.
sentences.zh: 重大的宪法变革是可以发生的。

sentences.en: So for those people on the left, Brexit has meant, I don't like the UK anymore.
sentences.zh: 所以对于左翼人士来说，脱欧意味着，我不再喜欢英国了。

sentences.en: For those people on the right, Brexit has shown, actually, maybe we could become independent.
sentences.zh: 对于右翼人士来说，脱欧表明，也许我们真的可以独立。

sentences.en: And a lot of the arguments over Brexit, about sovereignty, about looking after yourself, about rebuilding the economy from the bottom up, you know, those are the same ideas that
sentences.zh: 关于脱欧的许多争论，关于主权，关于自力更生，关于从底层重建经济，那些都是同样的思想，

sentences.en: can be applied to kind of, to Welsh independence, to Scottish independence.
sentences.zh: 可以应用于威尔士独立，应用于苏格兰独立。

sentences.en: And I know historians, I know from personal experience, historians are terrible, terrible predictors of the future.
sentences.zh: 我知道历史学家，我从个人经验中知道，历史学家是糟糕的未来预测者。

sentences.en: But if you were a betting man, do you think in our lifetime or our kind of children's lifetime, there will be an independent Welsh state?
sentences.zh: 但如果你是一个赌徒，你认为在我们有生之年，或者我们孩子那一代，会出现一个独立的威尔士国家吗？

sentences.en: Or do you think the union with England is too deep-seated to undo?
sentences.zh: 还是你认为与英格兰的联盟根深蒂固，无法拆解？

sentences.en: I think federalism of some form is inevitable.
sentences.zh: 我认为某种形式的联邦制是不可避免的。

sentences.en: I don't think the United Kingdom can survive in its current form.
sentences.zh: 我不认为联合王国能以目前的形式存续下去。

sentences.en: But the United Kingdom, like Wales, has proved remarkably resilient.
sentences.zh: 但联合王国，就像威尔士一样，证明了其非凡的韧性。

sentences.en: And if it is able to change and to adapt to the demands for recognition and equality in Wales and Scotland, then, you know, that may well happen.
sentences.zh: 如果它能够改变并适应威尔士和苏格兰对认可和平等的诉求，那么，这很可能会发生。

sentences.en: Ultimately, what happens to Wales will depend on what happens in Scotland.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，威尔士的命运将取决于苏格兰发生的事情。

sentences.en: We're doing this because of the England are playing Wales today.
sentences.zh: 我们做这个是因为今天英格兰队对阵威尔士队。

sentences.en: And there's all kinds of nationalist tab-thumping around the game.
sentences.zh: 比赛周围充满了各种民族主义的喧嚣。

sentences.en: But at the same time, as with rugby, so with football, English and Welsh players know each other incredibly well.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，就像橄榄球一样，足球也是如此，英格兰和威尔士的球员彼此非常了解。

sentences.en: The relationship between clubs and the national teams is very, very strong.
sentences.zh: 俱乐部和国家队之间的关系非常非常紧密。

sentences.en: And so in that sense, I guess this match does hold up quite a good mirror to the complexities
sentences.zh: 所以从这个意义上说，我想这场比赛确实很好地反映了英格兰和威尔士之间关系的复杂性

sentences.en: and the ambivalences of the relationships between England and Wales, because it's not all just about hostility and nationalist anthems and so on.
sentences.zh: 和矛盾心理，因为这不仅仅是关于敌意、民族主义国歌等等。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And, you know, we need to take a lot of things with a pinch of salt.
sentences.zh: 而且，我们需要对很多事情持保留态度。

sentences.en: You know, when people sing, you know, sort of patriotic songs, that doesn't mean they hate their neighbours.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当人们唱爱国歌曲时，并不意味着他们讨厌邻居。

sentences.en: You know, a lot of this is kind of pantomime in many ways.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在很多方面，这更像是一种哑剧。

sentences.en: You know, sports, football in particular, is very much like that.
sentences.zh: 体育，尤其是足球，非常像这样。

sentences.en: You know, the economies of Wales and England are very closely related.
sentences.zh: 威尔士和英格兰的经济联系非常紧密。

sentences.en: Most people in Wales have family, probably, in England.
sentences.zh: 威尔士的大多数人可能在英格兰都有亲戚。

sentences.en: Our societies are very closely related.
sentences.zh: 我们的社会联系非常紧密。

sentences.en: And that means that, you know, it is an inevitable that the two countries will drift apart.
sentences.zh: 这意味着两国不可避免地会渐行渐远。

sentences.en: And even if they do, even if there is Welsh independence, Scottish independence, you know, the United Kingdom will retain a cultural, you know, and a social function.
sentences.zh: 即使他们真的分开了，即使威尔士独立、苏格兰独立了，联合王国仍将保留文化和社会功能。

sentences.en: You know, we're a very small island and we're all too closely related, you know, to completely break away from each other.
sentences.zh: 我们是一个非常小的岛屿，我们联系太紧密了，无法完全脱离彼此。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a nice conclusion.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个很好的结论。

sentences.en: Now, one thing we didn't talk about, which I would like to quickly advertise to the listeners,
sentences.zh: 现在，有一件事我们没谈到，我想快速向听众宣传一下，

sentences.en: Martin did a brilliant programme on Radio 4 a couple of years ago.
sentences.zh: 马丁几年前在第四电台做了一个精彩的节目。

sentences.en: It was about the investiture of Prince Charles as Prince of Wales, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 是关于查尔斯王子受封威尔士亲王的，对吧？

sentences.en: That was the peg.
sentences.zh: 那是切入点。

sentences.en: But it also had this amazing story of this place called Truerrin, where there was a little village that was flooded to make way for a reservoir to serve the people of Liverpool,
sentences.zh: 但它也讲述了一个关于特里韦林（Tryweryn）这个地方的惊人故事，那里有一个小村庄为了修建水库供利物浦人民使用而被淹没，

sentences.en: which was a huge boost to...
sentences.zh: 这对……是一个巨大的推动。

sentences.en: The colonialists of Liverpool.
sentences.zh: 利物浦的殖民者们。

sentences.en: Yeah, the colonialists of Liverpool, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，利物浦的殖民者，没错。

sentences.en: That's not a phrase you often hear.
sentences.zh: 这不是你经常听到的短语。

sentences.en: So that was a lovely programme.
sentences.zh: 那是一个很棒的节目。

sentences.en: And for people who...
sentences.zh: 对于那些……

sentences.en: I imagine you might be able to find it on Radio 4.
sentences.zh: 我想你可能能在第四电台找到它。

sentences.en: It was actually really quite moving, Martin, I thought.
sentences.zh: 马丁，我觉得它实际上非常感人。

sentences.en: Is that...
sentences.zh: 是吗……

sentences.en: Am I being too purple about your programme?
sentences.zh: 我对你的节目评价太夸张了吗？

sentences.en: It was...
There was lovely music and very haunting and it wasn't like the rest is history.
sentences.zh: 有美妙的音乐，非常令人难忘，它不像《其余皆历史》那样。

sentences.en: It's a really powerful story because here was a small, entirely Welsh-speaking community that were moved from their homes to build a reservoir for England.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有力的故事，因为这里有一个小型的、完全讲威尔士语的社区，他们被迫搬离家园，为英格兰修建水库。

sentences.en: You know, this was about the loss of Welsh landscape.
sentences.zh: 这是关于威尔士景观的丧失。

sentences.en: This was about the loss of the Welsh community.
sentences.zh: 这是关于威尔士社区的丧失。

sentences.en: But it was also about the relationship between Wales and England because most, not all, but most of the Welsh MPs voted against it.
sentences.zh: 但这同时也是关于威尔士和英格兰之间关系的故事，因为大多数（不是全部，但大多数）威尔士议员投票反对它。

sentences.en: But it went through Parliament because there are more English MPs than Welsh MPs.
sentences.zh: 但它在议会通过了，因为英格兰议员比威尔士议员多。

sentences.en: And now it's become like this badge in Welsh culture.
sentences.zh: 现在它已经成为了威尔士文化中的一个标志。

sentences.en: And there's graffiti across Wales that says,
sentences.zh: 威尔士各地都有涂鸦写着：

sentences.en: Coveach Troueren, remember Troueren.
sentences.zh: 记住特里韦林（Cofiwch Dryweryn）。

sentences.en: And you're being asked to remember the loss of language, but also the inequality between Wales and England.
sentences.zh: 你被要求记住语言的丧失，以及威尔士和英格兰之间的不平等。

sentences.en: You know, some people describe the relationship as being like in bed with an elephant.
sentences.zh: 有些人形容这种关系就像和一头大象同床共枕。

sentences.en: Whether it's trying to crush you or not isn't the point.
sentences.zh: 它是否试图压垮你并不重要。

sentences.en: Inevitably, at some point, it will roll over and squash you.
sentences.zh: 不可避免地，在某个时刻，它会翻身把你压扁。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, let's hope that doesn't happen today, eh, Tom?
sentences.zh: 好吧，希望今天不会发生这种情况，汤姆？

sentences.en: Well, I reserve judgment on that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我对此保留意见。

sentences.en: I actually feel very conflicted about the England-Wales match because I am a quarter Welsh.
sentences.zh: 我实际上对英格兰对阵威尔士的比赛感到非常矛盾，因为我有四分之一的威尔士血统。

sentences.en: And I always like to root for the underdog.
sentences.zh: 而且我总是喜欢支持弱者。

sentences.en: I don't at all.
sentences.zh: 我一点也不。

sentences.en: Don't you?
sentences.zh: 你不吗？

sentences.en: You want England to absolutely hammer the Welsh.
sentences.zh: 你希望英格兰彻底痛击威尔士人。

sentences.en: It's funny, actually, because I sometimes make...
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，因为我有时会……

sentences.en: So the guy who used to run the books pages at the Sunday Times, he was a big rugby fan and an incredibly mild-mannered, sort of tolerant, nice person.
sentences.zh: 以前负责《星期日泰晤士报》书评版的那个人，他是个橄榄球迷，是个非常温和、宽容、好相处的人。

sentences.en: And he absolutely loathed the Welsh rugby team.
sentences.zh: 但他极其厌恶威尔士橄榄球队。

sentences.en: Absolutely loathed them.
sentences.zh: 极其厌恶他们。

sentences.en: Andrew Holgate.
sentences.zh: 安德鲁·霍尔盖特。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it's because he grew up in the 70s.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我想那是因为他在70年代长大。

sentences.en: And he just said, you know, they used to rub our faces in it year on year.
sentences.zh: 他刚才就说了，你知道，他们过去年复一年地让我们难堪。

sentences.en: So there you go, Martin.
sentences.zh: 所以就是这样，马丁。

sentences.en: That's a very bleak note on which to end.
sentences.zh: 以这样凄凉的基调结束真是太糟糕了。

sentences.en: No, I think we should just re-emphasize that it is, on the footballing level, so much pantomime.
sentences.zh: 不，我觉得我们应该再次强调，从足球层面来看，这真的太像闹剧了。

sentences.en: It is pantomime, yeah.
sentences.zh: 确实是闹剧，没错。

sentences.en: Basically.
sentences.zh: 基本上是这样。

sentences.en: And essentially, they're all friends.
sentences.zh: 而且本质上，他们都是朋友。

sentences.en: So being proud of your country doesn't mean you have to hate anyone else's.
sentences.zh: 所以，为你自己的国家感到自豪并不意味着你必须去憎恨别人的国家。

sentences.en: And on that note, on that bombshell.
sentences.zh: 带着这个想法，带着这个重磅消息。

sentences.en: Thank you so much, Martin.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你，马丁。

sentences.en: Thank you, everyone, for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢大家的收听。

sentences.en: And may the best team win.
sentences.zh: 愿最强的球队获胜。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Thanks for listening to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听《历史余味》。

sentences.zh: 如需收听加更剧集、抢先收听、无广告体验以及加入我们的聊天社区，请访问 restishistorypod.com 注册。
